Enable Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots in each workload account without setting retention locks.
items.exp: AWS Backup supports cross-account backup copies across AWS Organizations into an isolated dedicated backup account. Enabling AWS Backup Vault Lock in **Compliance mode** (after the cooling-off period expires) enforces WORM immutability: nobody—not even the root user of the workload account, the backup administrator, or AWS Support—can delete the recovery points or decrease their retention period before expiration.

items.q: A streaming analytics team is deploying a self-managed 21-node Apache Kafka and ZooKeeper cluster on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Region. Because Kafka already replicates each partition across multiple brokers, the team wants to ensure that groups of 3 brokers sit on completely isolated underlying AWS hardware racks (power, network switches, and host servers) across multiple Availability Zones so a single rack failure never takes down more than one group of brokers. Which EC2 placement strategy should they use?
opts: Cluster Placement Group
Spread Placement Group with 12 instances per Availability Zone
Partition Placement Group
Dedicated Hosts shared via AWS Resource Access Manager
items.exp: An EC2 Partition Placement Group divides instances into logical segments called partitions (up to 7 partitions per AZ), where each partition has its own independent set of racks, network, and power source. Unlike a Spread Placement Group (which is capped at 7 running instances per AZ), a Partition Placement Group scales to hundreds of instances while guaranteeing that rack-aware distributed systems like Kafka, HDFS, and Cassandra never lose more than one partition to a hardware rack failure.

items.q: Before Mammoth Capital launches its new Multi-AZ derivatives trading platform, the VP of Engineering wants to run controlled chaos engineering experiments in pre-production and production—such as injecting EC2 instance terminations, EBS I/O latency, and simulated AZ power interruptions—to prove that auto-healing and failover alarms work as designed. However, the experiment must immediately abort and roll back if an Amazon CloudWatch alarm detects customer checkout error rates exceeding 1%. Which AWS service provides this capability?
opts: AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Fault Injection Service (AWS FIS)
Amazon Inspector
items.exp: AWS Fault Injection Service (AWS FIS) is a managed chaos engineering service for running controlled fault-injection experiments on AWS workloads (EC2, ECS, EKS, RDS, networking). FIS integrates natively with Amazon CloudWatch Alarms as **Stop Conditions**: if a specified metric threshold (such as error rate > 1%) breaches during an experiment, FIS automatically halts the fault injection and restores normal state.

items.q: A retail bank exposes a loan-application webhook to hundreds of partner brokerages. The webhook writes records into a 20-year-old on-premises IBM mainframe over AWS Direct Connect. During mortgage rate drops, partner traffic spikes 40x to 12,000 requests per second, overwhelming the mainframe's maximum capacity of 250 transactions per second and causing connection timeouts. How can the Solutions Architect decouple the webhook so zero partner submissions are lost during traffic spikes and the mainframe processes records at a steady 250 requests per second?
opts: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with a direct AWS service integration that sends each payload straight into an Amazon SQS queue, and run a fixed fleet of ECS worker tasks that poll SQS and rate-limit themselves to 250 messages per second toward the mainframe.
Place an AWS Global Accelerator in front of the on-premises mainframe so TCP packets reach the mainframe faster.
Configure Amazon Route 53 Weighted Routing to drop 98% of incoming partner webhook requests whenever traffic exceeds 250 requests per second.
Replace the AWS Direct Connect link with an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device.
items.exp: This is the classic Queue-Based Load Leveling pattern: Amazon API Gateway can integrate directly with Amazon SQS (without even needing an intermediate Lambda function) to durably absorb bursts of 12,000 requests/second and return an immediate `202 Accepted` to partners. Downstream workers (ECS or Lambda with controlled concurrency) then drain the SQS queue at the exact 250 TPS pace the legacy mainframe can safely sustain.

items.q: A healthcare SaaS team deploys its patient portal using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Last month, a rolling deployment failed halfway through updating 10 EC2 instances, leaving 5 instances running v2.4 and 5 instances running broken v2.5 code, which required manual cleanup to recover. The team wants a deployment policy that guarantees a new version is verified on a fresh, separate set of instances in full before touching any existing production instances, and can roll back instantly by simply terminating the new instances if health checks fail. Which Elastic Beanstalk deployment policy should they choose?
opts: All at once
Rolling
Rolling with additional batch
Immutable
items.exp: An **Immutable** deployment in AWS Elastic Beanstalk launches a temporary, separate Auto Scaling group alongside the running production instances and deploys the new application version onto brand-new EC2 instances. Only after the new instances pass health checks over a verification period are they moved into the primary Auto Scaling group and the old instances terminated; if any health check fails, Elastic Beanstalk simply terminates the temporary instances, leaving the original production fleet 100% untouched.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's cloud security policy requires all production EC2 instances to run in private subnets across three Availability Zones (`us-east-1a`, `us-east-1b`, `us-east-1c`). Outbound HTTPS calls to third-party market data APIs currently route through a single NAT Gateway deployed in `us-east-1a`. During an architectural review, the Solutions Architect notices that if `us-east-1a` experiences an Availability Zone outage, EC2 instances in `us-east-1b` and `us-east-1c` will also lose all outbound internet connectivity. What is the correct fix to achieve full AZ independence?
opts: Attach an Elastic IP address to every private EC2 instance in `us-east-1b` and `us-east-1c`.

Deploy a NAT Gateway in the public subnet of EACH of the three Availability Zones, create a separate private route table for each AZ, and point each AZ's private route table `0.0.0.0/0` route to the NAT Gateway in that same AZ.
Replace the NAT Gateway with an Egress-Only Internet Gateway for the IPv4 private subnets.
Place the single NAT Gateway inside an EC2 Auto Scaling group spanning all three Availability Zones.
items.exp: Although a managed NAT Gateway is redundant within its own Availability Zone, it cannot survive the failure of that entire AZ. For true Multi-AZ fault isolation (and to eliminate cross-AZ data transfer charges), AWS recommends deploying one NAT Gateway in a public subnet in each Availability Zone and configuring an AZ-specific private route table so private instances in `az-a`, `az-b`, and `az-c` each egress through their local AZ's NAT Gateway.

items.q: Mammoth Capital runs a latency-sensitive options pricing database on an `r6i.16xlarge` Nitro-based EC2 instance backed by a single Amazon EBS volume. During market open, the database requires a sustained 180,000 IOPS, 3,200 MB/s of throughput, and sub-millisecond disk latency with 99.999% volume durability. Which single EBS volume type can deliver 180,000 IOPS and 3,200 MB/s without striping multiple volumes?
opts: Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD (`gp3`) with Burst Credits enabled
Amazon EBS Throughput Optimized HDD (`st1`)
Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io2` Block Express)
Amazon EBS Cold HDD (`sc1`)
items.exp: Amazon EBS `io2` Block Express is built on next-generation SAN storage architecture for Nitro-based EC2 instances. A single `io2` Block Express volume supports up to 256,000 IOPS, up to 4,000 MB/s of throughput, up to 64 TiB capacity, sub-millisecond average latency, and 99.999% durability—easily handling 180,000 IOPS without software RAID striping.

items.q: Every morning at 06:30 EST before the stock market opens, Mammoth Capital restores a 12 TiB production Amazon EBS snapshot to create four fresh pre-trade simulation volumes. However, during the first 45 minutes of simulation runs, disk read latency spikes to 35 ms whenever a worker reads a data block on the newly restored EBS volume for the first time. Which AWS feature eliminates this first-read initialization penalty so the restored volumes deliver full provisioned IOPS immediately upon attachment?
opts: Enable Amazon EBS Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) on the source snapshot in the target Availability Zones.
Convert the EBS volumes from `gp3` to `sc1` Cold HDD before taking the snapshot.
Enable EBS Encryption by default using an AWS KMS asymmetric customer managed key.
Mount the EBS snapshot directly over NFS using Amazon EFS Elastic Throughput.
items.exp: EBS volumes restored from snapshots ordinarily pull data blocks lazily from Amazon S3 in the background, causing a significant I/O latency hit on the first read of each block (the initialization penalty). Enabling Amazon EBS Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) on a snapshot for specific Availability Zones pre-warms the blocks at creation time so every restored volume delivers 100% of its provisioned performance instantly.

items.q: A global fintech news portal serves 85,000 requests per second through Amazon CloudFront. Before routing requests to the cache or origin, the team needs to normalize URL paths to lowercase, strip tracking query parameters (`utm_*`), and rewrite the `Accept-Language` header into a two-letter locale cookie. Each invocation runs in under 0.3 milliseconds, needs no network or file system access, and must be as cost-effective and low-latency as possible. Where should this logic run?
opts: AWS Lambda@Edge triggered on the `origin-response` event in `us-east-1`
CloudFront Functions triggered on the `viewer-request` event
An Amazon ECS Fargate reverse-proxy cluster running behind an Application Load Balancer
An AWS Step Functions Express Workflow invoked via API Gateway
items.exp: CloudFront Functions is a lightweight JavaScript runtime deployed directly to all 600+ CloudFront edge locations (rather than regional edge caches). It is purpose-built for short-lived (<1 ms), high-scale `viewer-request` and `viewer-response` manipulations like URL rewrites, header normalization, and cache-key cleanup at a fraction of the cost and latency of Lambda@Edge.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's quantitative research team downloads 250 GB historical market replay files from an Amazon S3 bucket to `c7i.16xlarge` EC2 instances in the same Region (`us-east-1`, connected via an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint). Currently, their Python script downloads each 250 GB file using a single-threaded `GetObject` stream, taking over 35 minutes and utilizing less than 5% of the instance's 25 Gbps network card. How can they cut the download time to under 90 seconds without changing storage services?
opts: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and download via the `s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com` endpoint.

Modify the download client (or use the AWS CRT / `s3transfer` library) to issue concurrent, multi-threaded HTTP `Range` (`Byte-Range`) GET requests across multiple TCP connections and reassemble the parts in memory/disk.
Move the 250 GB files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
Place an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway between the EC2 instance and the S3 bucket.
items.exp: A single S3 HTTP GET stream is limited by single-connection TCP throughput. By issuing concurrent **Byte-Range Fetches** (`Range: bytes=0-67108863`, etc.) across dozens of parallel threads—which the AWS SDK Common Runtime (CRT) and `aws s3 cp` do automatically when configured—the EC2 instance aggregates throughput across many S3 storage servers simultaneously and saturates its 25 Gbps NIC.

items.q: A genomics startup runs containerized bioinformatics pipelines on Amazon ECS that share reference genome files and intermediate outputs on an Amazon EFS file system. Their workload is completely unpredictable: the file system sits idle at 5 MB/s for hours, then suddenly bursts to 2.5 GB/s of read throughput for 20 minutes whenever a sequencing batch arrives, causing their old Bursting Throughput file system to run out of burst credits and stall. The team does not want to pay for 2.5 GB/s of Provisioned Throughput 24/7. Which EFS throughput mode should they configure?
opts: Bursting Throughput mode with a daily cron job that writes dummy files to earn burst credits
Provisioned Throughput mode set permanently to 3,000 MB/s
Elastic Throughput mode
Migrate the file system to Amazon EFS One Zone with Bursting Throughput
items.exp: Amazon EFS **Elastic Throughput** mode is designed specifically for spiky, unpredictable workloads. It automatically scales throughput up (up to several GB/s per Region) and down instantly on demand with no burst credits to track and no capacity to over-provision—you pay only for the exact bytes of metadata and data read or written.

items.q: Mammoth Capital ingests real-time equity tick data into an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream with 20 shards. Originally, two applications consumed the stream with sub-200ms latency. Over the past year, seven more risk, surveillance, and pricing microservices were added as consumers of the same stream. Now all nine consumers experience `ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded` exceptions and 1.5-second lag spikes because they compete for each shard's shared 2 MB/s read limit. What is the MOST effective way to give every consumer its own isolated 2 MB/s read pipe per shard with ~70ms push delivery?
opts: Register each of the nine applications as an Enhanced Fan-Out consumer using the Kinesis Consumer API (`SubscribeToShard` over HTTP/2).
Switch the consumers from polling every 250ms to polling every 10ms using standard `GetRecords` calls.
Enable Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS (`SSE-KMS`) on the Kinesis Data Stream.
Replace the Kinesis Data Stream with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) FIFO topic.
items.exp: With standard `GetRecords` polling, all consumers of a Kinesis shard share a single 2 MB/s read limit and 5 reads/second cap. Registering consumers with **Enhanced Fan-Out** allocates a dedicated 2 MB/s read pipe *per consumer per shard* and pushes records over HTTP/2 via `SubscribeToShard`, achieving ~70ms propagation latency regardless of how many other consumers read the stream.

items.q: A legal-tech SaaS platform stores 180 million court filings in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. Users complain that searching across document bodies for fuzzy keyword matches, proximity phrases, and faceted filters (`ILIKE '%antitrust%'`) takes 25–40 seconds and pegs the RDS CPU at 100%. The team needs a managed search engine that delivers sub-second full-text search, typo tolerance, and relevance scoring while keeping older historical index data cost-effective. Which AWS service should they add?
opts: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
Amazon OpenSearch Service (with UltraWarm and Cold storage tiers for older indices)
Amazon Neptune
AWS Glue DataBrew
items.exp: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides distributed inverted indices built on Apache Lucene, delivering sub-second full-text search, fuzzy matching, stemming, relevance scoring, and faceted aggregations across hundreds of millions of documents. Its UltraWarm and Cold storage tiers (backed by Amazon S3 with local caching) let teams retain years of searchable indices at a fraction of hot SSD node cost.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's financial crime unit is building a real-time anti-money-laundering (AML) engine to detect circular wire-transfer rings. Given a suspicious account ID, the system must traverse 6 to 8 hops of shared device fingerprints, beneficial owners, shell companies, and intermediary bank transfers in under 50 milliseconds. In their prototype on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, a 7-level self-join query takes 19 seconds and times out under load. Which purpose-built AWS database is optimized for this query pattern?
opts: Amazon Timestream
Amazon Redshift with `EVEN` table distribution
Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (QLDB)
Amazon Neptune
items.exp: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database optimized for storing billions of relationships and traversing multi-hop property graphs or RDF graphs with millisecond latency. Using Apache TinkerPop Gremlin or openCypher, 6-to-8-hop fraud-ring and entity-link traversals execute in milliseconds without the exponential index-join explosion of relational databases.

items.q: A smart-grid energy provider collects voltage, frequency, and phase-angle readings every second from 2.4 million smart meters across North America. They need to ingest 2.4 million data points per second, run real-time interpolation and time-window downsampling queries over the last 48 hours of data with millisecond latency, and automatically tier data older than 48 hours to cheaper magnetic storage for 5-year trend analysis without managing database servers or partition tables. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this workload?
opts: Amazon Timestream
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
Amazon RDS for MySQL with Read Replicas
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive queried directly via S3 Select
items.exp: Amazon Timestream is a serverless, purpose-built time-series database that ingests millions of time-stamped data points per second, provides built-in time-series functions (interpolation, smoothing, binned aggregation), and automatically tiers recent hot data from its in-memory store to a cost-optimized magnetic store based on lifecycle policies you define.

items.q: An IoT fleet management company writes sensor status updates from 500,000 delivery trucks into an Amazon DynamoDB table provisioned with 20,000 Write Capacity Units (WCUs). The table uses `StatusDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) as the Partition Key and `TruckID#Timestamp` as the Sort Key. Even though total write traffic is only 3,500 writes per second—well below the 20,000 WCU table limit—the application experiences constant `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` errors all day. What is the root cause and how should the schema be redesigned?
opts: DynamoDB cannot handle more than 1,000 writes per second per table; migrate the workload to Amazon RDS for SQL Server.

All writes for a given day share the exact same Partition Key value (`StatusDate`), creating a single hot partition (capped at 1,000 WCUs per physical partition); redesign the Partition Key to a high-cardinality attribute such as `TruckID` (or append a write-sharding suffix like `StatusDate#0..19`).
The Sort Key string is too short; pad the Sort Key with 4 KB of random whitespace.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) so write requests are absorbed without ever being written to the base DynamoDB table.
items.exp: Every single physical partition in Amazon DynamoDB has a hard hardware limit of **1,000 Write Capacity Units (WCUs)** (and 3,000 RCUs) per second. When `StatusDate` (`2026-10-19`) is used as the Partition Key, 100% of today's 3,500 writes/sec hammer the exact same single physical partition while the other 19 partitions sit completely idle. Using a high-cardinality Partition Key like `TruckID` (or write-sharding `StatusDate#N` across 10–20 random or calculated suffixes) distributes writes evenly across all partitions.

items.q: A SaaS analytics company runs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with one Primary Writer (`db.r6g.4xlarge`) and four Aurora Replicas (`db.r6g.2xlarge`). During business hours, a fleet of 60 EC2 reporting workers connects to the cluster's single built-in Reader Endpoint using persistent connection pools of 50 connections each. Because the Aurora Reader Endpoint uses DNS round-robin with a short TTL to return a single replica's IP address per DNS lookup, whenever two new Aurora Replicas scale out during a traffic spike, existing long-lived connection pools stay pinned to the original four replicas while the two new replicas sit nearly idle. How can the team achieve balanced request distribution across all Aurora Replicas without rewriting the application's database driver?
opts: Place Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the Aurora cluster (using a read-only proxy endpoint) so RDS Proxy multiplexes client connections at the transaction/statement level across all active Aurora Replicas.
Change the Route 53 public domain TTL to 86,400 seconds (24 hours).
Delete the Aurora Reader Endpoint and hardcode the IP address of the first replica in `/etc/hosts`.
Replace the Aurora Replicas with an Amazon S3 Static Website endpoint.
items.exp: The standard Aurora Reader Endpoint resolves at the DNS layer (returning one replica IP per DNS query), so applications that open long-lived connection pools only resolve DNS once at startup and can skew traffic when replicas scale out. Placing **Amazon RDS Proxy** (with a read-only endpoint) in front of the cluster maintains a shared connection pool to all underlying Aurora Replicas and distributes individual SQL queries evenly across healthy replicas as they scale in or out.

items.q: Inside an Amazon Redshift data warehouse, Mammoth Capital frequently joins a massive 4-billion-row `trade_executions` fact table with an 80-million-row `order_books` fact table on the `order_id` column, and also joins both tables with a small 2,500-row `exchange_venues` dimension table. Query execution plans show `DS_BCAST_INNER` and `DS_DIST_BOTH` network redistribution steps taking 85% of total query runtime as slices shuffle gigabytes of rows across the network on every join. Which Redshift table distribution style strategy will eliminate network shuffling for these joins?
opts: Set `DISTSTYLE EVEN` on all three tables so rows are sprayed round-robin across every slice.
Set `DISTSTYLE ALL` on the 4-billion-row `trade_executions` table so a full copy of all 4 billion rows is duplicated on every compute node.

Configure `DISTSTYLE KEY` with `DISTKEY (order_id)` on both `trade_executions` and `order_books` to co-locate matching `order_id` rows on the same node slice, and configure `DISTSTYLE ALL` on the small 2,500-row `exchange_venues` dimension table.
Disable Sort Keys and store all three tables in a single unindexed JSON text column.
items.exp: Setting `DISTSTYLE KEY` on the shared join column (`order_id`) for both large fact tables guarantees that rows with the same `order_id` are already physically co-located on the exact same compute node slice (`DS_DIST_NONE`), eliminating cross-node network shuffling during the join. Setting `DISTSTYLE ALL` on the small slowly changing 2,500-row dimension table places a copy on every node so joins with it are also local.

items.q: A healthcare records startup runs an on-premises hospital imaging system that generates 8 TB of new DICOM X-ray files every week. Radiologists at the hospital need sub-5ms local LAN read latency over SMB/NFS for X-rays taken within the last 7 days, while older studies must be durably stored in Amazon S3 as standard native S3 objects so cloud-based AWS HealthImaging and SageMaker ML pipelines can read them directly from the S3 bucket. Which AWS service meets BOTH the local LAN cache performance and direct native S3 object access requirements?
opts: AWS Storage Gateway — Volume Gateway in Cached mode
AWS Storage Gateway — Volume Gateway in Stored mode
AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway — Amazon S3 File Gateway
items.exp: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an SMB or NFS mount point to on-premises servers backed by a local disk cache on the gateway VM/appliance for sub-5ms LAN reads of recently accessed files, while asynchronously writing each file into Amazon S3 as a **1:1 native S3 object** that cloud services like SageMaker and Athena can access directly.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's user-profile microservice reads customer KYC records from an Amazon RDS database backed by an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster. Currently, the team uses only Lazy Loading (Cache-Aside) without TTLs: whenever a KYC officer updates a customer's margin limit in RDS, the Redis cache continues serving the stale old limit until the cache node is manually flushed. Conversely, when the team switched to pure Write-Through caching for every database table, 92% of the Redis memory filled up with cold historical audit rows that are never read again. What caching strategy gives the BEST balance of fresh data and optimal cache memory utilization?
opts: Use Lazy Loading (Cache-Aside) for general read paths combined with Write-Through (or explicit cache invalidation/update on write) specifically for hot profile keys, and configure an appropriate Time-to-Live (TTL) on all cached keys.
Disable ElastiCache completely and query RDS using `SELECT *` without indexes.
Set the Redis TTL to 10 milliseconds on every key so the cache expires before a second user can read it.
Replace ElastiCache for Redis with Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
items.exp: Combining **Lazy Loading** (so only requested items occupy memory) with targeted **Write-Through** updates (or immediate key invalidation when a KYC record is modified) and a sensible **TTL** expiration policy is the industry-standard pattern: hot reads are always fast and up to date, stale keys self-expire if an invalidation is ever missed, and cold rows don't bloat cache RAM.

items.q: A high-frequency foreign exchange (FX) venue runs UDP market-data gateways and TCP FIX order gateways on EC2 instances behind a load balancer. They need the load balancer to handle millions of UDP and TCP packets per second with ultra-low latency, give partners one static IP address per Availability Zone for firewall allow-lists, and preserve the client's original source IP address at the packet level without parsing HTTP `X-Forwarded-For` headers. Which AWS load balancer should they use?
opts: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
Classic Load Balancer (CLB) configured in HTTP mode
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
Network Load Balancer (NLB)
items.exp: Amazon **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** operates at Layer 4, handles millions of TCP and UDP requests per second with ultra-low latency, offers one static (or Elastic) IP per Availability Zone, and preserves the client's source IP in the IP header for TCP and UDP listeners when targets are registered by instance ID. (If you terminate TLS on the NLB instead, use Proxy Protocol v2 to pass the client IP.)

items.q: Mammoth Capital runs a fleet of 150 stateless Go and Python microservices on x86_64 (`c6i.4xlarge` and `m6i.4xlarge`) EC2 instances and ECS Fargate tasks. During a performance and cost audit, the Solutions Architect notes that all dependencies are open-source multi-arch Linux packages with no x86-specific assembly binaries. Which compute migration will improve price-performance by up to 40% while increasing per-core energy efficiency?
opts: Migrate the workloads to `mac2.metal` EC2 Dedicated Hosts.

Migrate the EC2 instances and ECS Fargate tasks to AWS Graviton3/Graviton4 (`64-bit Arm` architecture) instances such as `c7g.4xlarge` and `m7g.4xlarge` by building multi-architecture container images in Amazon ECR.
Downgrade the fleet to previous-generation `t2.micro` burstable instances.
Move the stateless microservices onto AWS Snowcone edge devices.
items.exp: AWS Graviton processors (`c7g`, `m7g`, `r7g`, `c8g`) are custom-built 64-bit Arm Neoverse CPUs engineered by AWS that deliver up to 40% better price-performance than comparable x86 instances. Because Go, Python, Java, Node.js, and Docker multi-arch images compile cleanly to `linux/arm64`, migrating stateless microservices to Graviton on EC2 or Fargate is one of the highest-leverage performance-efficiency wins on SAA-C03.

items.q: An ad-tech platform processes real-time bidding streams on `c5n.18xlarge` EC2 instances running Ubuntu Server, similar to a high-throughput Proxmox or bare-metal packet router. Each instance processes 1.2 million network packets per second (PPS). The networking team notices softirq CPU bottlenecks inside the guest OS kernel and wants to verify that the instances are using AWS hardware-assisted Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) for maximum PPS, lowest jitter, and up to 100 Gbps network bandwidth. Which EC2 feature provides this capability on modern Nitro instances?
opts: Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Enhanced Networking
AWS Direct Connect Public VIF
VPC Peering with ClassicLink
Elastic IP Address remapping
items.exp: **Enhanced Networking** using the **Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)** uses Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) to give the guest OS direct hardware-level access to the network card without hypervisor translation overhead. This delivers significantly higher packet-per-second (PPS) performance, consistently lower inter-instance latency, and up to 100–200 Gbps of network bandwidth at no additional charge.

items.q: A bioinformatics lab runs nightly genome alignment jobs using Docker containers. Each batch consists of 40,000 independent whole-genome alignment tasks that require varying combinations of vCPUs, RAM, and GPU accelerators. The lab currently keeps an idle 80-node Amazon EKS cluster running 24/7 just to run the 3-hour nightly batch, wasting $45,000 per month. Which AWS service will automatically queue the 40,000 jobs, dynamically provision the optimal mix of Spot and On-Demand EC2/Fargate compute environments when jobs arrive, and scale the compute nodes down to zero when the queue is empty?
opts: AWS Elastic Beanstalk Worker Environment with a static minimum of 80 instances
Amazon Lightsail Containers
AWS AppSync
AWS Batch
items.exp: **AWS Batch** is purpose-built for large-scale batch computing and HPC workloads. It manages job queues, dependency ordering (`array jobs`), and retry policies, and dynamically provisions and scales the underlying EC2 (Spot or On-Demand) or AWS Fargate compute environments up to thousands of vCPUs when jobs are submitted and right back down to zero when the queue drains.

items.q: Mammoth Capital exposes a REST API through Amazon API Gateway that returns reference exchange-rate tables and stock market holiday calendars. Although those reference datasets only change once every 15 minutes, 4,500 mobile client requests per second trigger the backing AWS Lambda function and query the Amazon RDS database for the exact same JSON payload. What is the SIMPLEST way to reduce backend Lambda invocations and cut API response latency from 120 ms to under 15 ms?
opts: Enable API Gateway stage caching with a 900-second (15-minute) TTL on the reference `GET` methods.
Rewrite the AWS Lambda function in assembly language and deploy it in 12 AWS Regions.
Place an AWS Storage Gateway in front of Amazon API Gateway.
Increase the RDS database instance size from `db.m6g.large` to `db.x2iedn.32xlarge`.
items.exp: Amazon API Gateway provides a built-in, fully managed **API Cache** per stage (powered by dedicated cache capacity with configurable encrypted storage and TTL up to 3,600 seconds). Enabling caching with a 900-second TTL on the reference `GET` endpoints serves repeated requests directly from API Gateway in milliseconds without invoking Lambda or hitting RDS.

items.q: A document processing company runs a fleet of EC2 worker instances in an Auto Scaling group that pulls PDF OCR tasks from an Amazon SQS queue. Each PDF takes roughly 45 seconds to process. Originally, the team configured the Auto Scaling group to scale on average EC2 `CPUUtilization > 70%`, but whenever 50,000 PDFs arrive at once, the existing 4 workers hit 80% CPU and only add 1 or 2 instances while the SQS backlog takes 6 hours to drain. How should the Solutions Architect configure the Auto Scaling policy so the fleet scales proportionally to the actual queue backlog and drains bursts within 10 minutes?
opts: Scale the Auto Scaling group based on `NetworkOut` bytes instead of `CPUUtilization`.
Use a Scheduled Scaling policy that adds 10 instances every Tuesday at noon.

Configure a Target Tracking scaling policy based on a custom metric calculated by dividing the SQS `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible` by the Auto Scaling group's `GroupInServiceInstances` (the **backlog per instance** metric), targeting the acceptable backlog per worker.
Replace the Auto Scaling group with a single `t3.nano` EC2 instance.
items.exp: CPU utilization only tells you that existing workers are busy—it does not tell you whether there are 10 messages or 100,000 messages waiting in the SQS queue. AWS recommends scaling queue-worker Auto Scaling groups using a Target Tracking policy on the **Backlog Per Instance** metric (`ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible / GroupInServiceInstances`), compared against the **Acceptable Backlog Per Capacity Unit** (acceptable latency divided by average processing time per message).

items.q: Mammoth Capital's quantitative trading desk runs a competitive real-time market simulator accessed by traders in Tokyo, London, and New York over custom persistent UDP and TCP sockets. Traders complain that ISP BGP routing flaps across the public internet cause jitter spikes of 80–200 ms, and whenever the primary `us-east-1` Application/Network Load Balancer fails over to `eu-west-1`, client OS and ISP DNS resolvers ignore the 60-second Route 53 TTL and stay stuck on the dead IP for up to 10 minutes. Which AWS service provides two static Anycast IPv4 addresses, ingests client UDP/TCP traffic onto the AWS global fiber backbone at the nearest edge location, and fails over across Regions in under 30 seconds without relying on client DNS cache expiration?
opts: Amazon CloudFront with an S3 static website origin
Amazon Route 53 Geolocation routing with a 5-second TTL
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Transfer Family
items.exp: **AWS Global Accelerator** allocates two static Anycast IP addresses announced from AWS edge locations worldwide. It supports both **TCP and UDP** protocols, routes traffic immediately onto the congestion-free AWS global network backbone, and performs continuous endpoint health checks—rerouting traffic to healthy regional NLB/ALB/EC2 endpoints in under 30 seconds with zero dependency on client DNS TTL caching.

items.q: A machine learning team at Mammoth Capital trains large financial language models on a cluster of 16 `p4d.24xlarge` GPU instances in `us-east-1`. Their 80 TB training dataset of tokenized SEC filings resides in an Amazon S3 bucket. During training epochs, the GPUs sit idle 40% of the time waiting for millions of small binary shard files to be read over the S3 HTTP API. The team wants a high-performance POSIX file system that transparently lazy-loads objects from the S3 bucket on demand, caches them across NVMe/SSD storage at hundreds of GB/s of throughput with sub-millisecond latency, and can export final model checkpoints right back to the S3 bucket. Which service should they deploy?
opts: Amazon EBS Cold HDD (`sc1`)
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
Amazon WorkDocs
Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with the Amazon S3 data repository
items.exp: **Amazon FSx for Lustre** is a fully managed parallel POSIX file system purpose-built for machine learning and HPC workloads, delivering hundreds of GB/s of throughput and millions of IOPS with sub-millisecond latency. When linked to an **Amazon S3 data repository**, FSx for Lustre presents S3 objects as POSIX files, transparently lazy-loads training shards into the high-speed Lustre file system on first read (or pre-loads them), and exports updated checkpoints back to S3.

items.q: A retail analytics company runs an Apache Spark ETL pipeline for 90 minutes every evening to aggregate clickstream logs from Amazon S3 into Parquet tables. Currently, an engineer manually launches a 30-node Amazon EMR cluster on EC2 every afternoon, guesses the cluster size, and often forgets to terminate it overnight—or sizes it too small when traffic doubles on promo days, causing the job to miss its SLA. The team wants to run their standard open-source Spark jobs without provisioning, configuring, tuning, or terminating EC2 cluster nodes, while having compute workers scale up and down automatically within seconds based on each Spark stage's parallelism. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
opts: Amazon EMR on EC2 using On-Demand Dedicated Hosts with manual resizing
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a stored procedure
Amazon EMR Serverless
Amazon Lightsail virtual private servers
items.exp: **Amazon EMR Serverless** is a serverless deployment option inside Amazon EMR that runs open-source big data frameworks (such as Apache Spark and Apache Hive) without requiring you to configure, provision, optimize, or manage EC2 clusters. It automatically provisions and scales workers at each stage of your Spark job and shuts them down immediately when idle, with optional pre-initialized capacity for instant startup.

items.q: Mammoth Capital allows senior platform engineers to create IAM roles for new microservices deployed on ECS and Lambda. However, the CISO wants a technical guardrail ensuring that even if a platform engineer has iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy permissions, no role they create can ever grant permissions broader than a specific company-wide security ceiling (for example, preventing any newly created role from calling kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion or iam:*). Which IAM mechanism enforces this ceiling on the roles the engineers create?
opts: Attach an IAM permissions boundary policy to the platform engineers' own IAM user/role identities.

Configure an IAM policy on the platform engineers' role that allows iam:CreateRole and iam:PutRolePolicy only when the Condition iam:PermissionsBoundary equals the ARN of the company security ceiling policy.
Apply an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Root OU that denies iam:CreateRole unless MFA is present.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share a read-only IAM role template across the organization.
items.exp: To safely delegate role creation, you attach an IAM policy to the delegating engineer that requires the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition key on iam:CreateRole (and prevents deleting or detaching that boundary). That forces every new role the engineer creates to carry the permissions boundary, which caps the maximum effective permissions that new role can ever exercise.

items.q: Mammoth Capital hired an external security vendor to audit their AWS environment. The vendor runs a multi-tenant SaaS scanner in the vendor's own AWS account and asks Mammoth to create an IAM role trusting the vendor's AWS account ID. A security architect warns that another customer of the same vendor could trick the vendor's scanner into assuming Mammoth's role (the 'confused deputy' problem). How should Mammoth configure the IAM role's trust policy to prevent this?
opts: Require the sts:ExternalId condition key in the IAM role's trust policy set to a unique secret identifier generated by the vendor for Mammoth.
Add the aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key set to Mammoth Capital's AWS Organization ID in the trust policy.
Replace the cross-account IAM role with long-lived IAM user access keys rotated every 90 days via AWS Secrets Manager.
Restrict the IAM role's trust policy using the aws:SecureTransport condition key set to true.
items.exp: The sts:ExternalId condition in an IAM role trust policy solves the cross-account confused deputy problem when a third-party SaaS uses a shared AWS account. Even if another customer guesses Mammoth's role ARN, the vendor's AssumeRole call on behalf of that other customer will pass the wrong ExternalId and be denied by STS.

items.q: After migrating a legacy trading application from an on-premises Ubuntu server to Amazon EC2, the team notices the instance profile still has the AdministratorAccess policy attached from initial testing. The security team wants to replace it with a least-privilege IAM policy based on the exact AWS services and actions the application actually called over the past 60 days, without manually combing through millions of raw log lines. Which native AWS feature accomplishes this?
opts: AWS Trusted Advisor Security checks
IAM Access Analyzer policy generation based on AWS CloudTrail activity
Amazon Inspector runtime network reachability assessment
AWS Artifact compliance policy generator
items.exp: IAM Access Analyzer can analyze up to 90 days of AWS CloudTrail logs for a specific IAM role or user and automatically generate a fine-grained, least-privilege IAM policy template containing only the services and actions that principal actually invoked.

items.q: Mammoth Capital manages 40 AWS accounts under AWS Organizations and uses AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) federated with Okta. Currently, every time a new project squad is formed, an admin has to create new Permission Sets and update dozens of IAM policies to grant access to that squad's DynamoDB tables and S3 prefixes. How can the architect redesign access control so new squads automatically gain access to their own tagged resources without modifying IAM policies?
opts: Enable Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) in IAM Identity Center by passing Okta department/project attributes as session tags and writing a single IAM policy comparing ${aws:PrincipalTag/Project} to ${aws:ResourceTag/Project}.
Create an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) for each squad and attach it directly to the individual IAM users.
Deploy an AWS Directory Service Simple AD cluster in every AWS account and map POSIX group IDs to S3 bucket ACLs.
Use IAM Access Keys stored in SSM Parameter Store with tag-based KMS key grants.
items.exp: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) with IAM Identity Center maps identity attributes from the external IdP (Okta) into STS session tags (aws:PrincipalTag). A single permission set policy can then grant access whenever the principal's Project tag matches the resource's Project tag, scaling to new squads with zero policy edits.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's AWS Organization has a 'Production' Organizational Unit (OU) containing ten member accounts. To meet regulatory rules, the CISO wants to ensure that no one in any Production member account—including the member account's IAM administrators and even the member account's root user—can ever disable Amazon GuardDuty or delete AWS CloudTrail trails. How should the Solutions Architect implement this?
opts: Attach an explicit Deny IAM policy to the OrganizationAccountAccessRole in each member account.

Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) with an explicit Deny on guardduty:DeleteDetector, guardduty:DisassociateFromMasterAccount, cloudtrail:StopLogging, and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail to the Production OU.
Configure an AWS Config rule in each member account that sends an SNS email whenever root user credentials are used.
Enable IAM Permissions Boundaries on the root user of each member account in the Production OU.
items.exp: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) apply to all principals inside a member account, including IAM admins and the member account's root user. An explicit Deny in an SCP attached to the Production OU cannot be overridden by any local IAM policy inside the member account.

items.q: Mammoth Capital stores client brokerage statements in an Amazon S3 bucket. To pass an SEC Rule 17a-4 compliance audit, the security team must prove two things: first, every single encrypt and decrypt event on the statements' encryption key is recorded in AWS CloudTrail with the caller's identity; second, the company can immediately revoke access to the key material itself within seconds while retaining the ability to restore the exact same key bytes later if it was a false alarm. Which encryption option meets both requirements?
opts: SSE-S3 (Server-Side Encryption with Amazon S3-Managed Keys)
SSE-KMS using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) with imported key material (BYOK)
SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys)
SSE-KMS using the AWS-managed key (aws/s3)
items.exp: SSE-KMS logs every key usage event in AWS CloudTrail, and using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) with imported key material lets you call kms:DeleteImportedKeyMaterial to immediately render objects undecryptable within seconds (unlike the minimum 7-day waiting period of standard KMS key deletion) while letting you re-import the exact same key material later.

items.q: A financial compliance regulation requires Mammoth Capital to retain trade-confirmation PDFs in Amazon S3 in a Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) state for 7 years. During that 7-year retention window, no user—not even the AWS account root user—may overwrite or delete any PDF, or shorten the retention period. However, if the SEC opens an active investigation into a specific client account, the legal team must be able to freeze specific PDFs indefinitely until the investigation concludes, even if their 7-year timer expires in the meantime. How should S3 be configured?
opts: Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a 7-year retention period, and apply an Object Lock Legal Hold to the specific objects under SEC investigation.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode with a 7-year retention period, and attach an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to Glacier Deep Archive.
Enable S3 Versioning with MFA Delete enabled on the bucket and restrict s3:DeleteObjectVersion via a Bucket Policy.
Copy the PDFs into an AWS Backup vault using a Warm Storage tier without vault lock.
items.exp: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode enforces strict WORM protection where no principal—including the AWS account root user—can delete the object or shorten the retention period. Applying a Legal Hold adds an independent, indefinite freeze on specific objects that stays in effect until explicitly removed by a user with s3:PutObjectLegalHold permissions.

items.q: Mammoth Capital has a central 500 TB S3 data lake bucket shared by 25 internal analytics teams across multiple VPCs. Each team needs access to its own prefix inside the bucket, and the bucket policy has grown close to the 20 KB size limit, making it brittle and risky to edit. Additionally, the security team wants to enforce that the Quantitative Research team's requests can only originate from their specific Research VPC. What is the cleanest way to scale and isolate access management for this bucket?
opts: Create dedicated S3 Access Points for each team with tailored access point policies, and configure the Quantitative Research team's S3 Access Point to be restricted to their Research VPC.
Split the 500 TB bucket into 25 separate S3 buckets and configure S3 Cross-Region Replication between all 25 buckets.
Enable S3 Object ACLs on all 500 TB of objects and manage individual IAM user grants per object.
Deploy 25 separate NAT Gateways and filter S3 prefix paths inside the VPC Network ACLs.
items.exp: S3 Access Points let you break a monolithic bucket policy into up to thousands of discrete, named network endpoints—each with its own independent access point policy (up to 20 KB each) and optional VPC-only origin restriction.

items.q: Mammoth Academy sells premium video courses where each 2-hour lecture is encoded into HLS streaming format, consisting of a master `.m3u8` playlist and over 1,200 individual `.ts` video segment files stored in a private Amazon S3 bucket behind Amazon CloudFront. Once a subscriber logs in, they should be able to stream the entire lecture seamlessly for 4 hours without the backend server having to rewrite the `.m3u8` playlist or generate 1,200 separate signatures. Which mechanism should the architect use?
opts: CloudFront Signed Cookies scoped with a custom policy to the lecture's directory path prefix and a 4-hour expiration.
S3 Pre-Signed URLs generated individually for each of the 1,200 `.ts` files when the page loads.
CloudFront Origin Access Identity (OAI) with public unauthenticated access enabled on the CloudFront distribution.
AWS Secrets Manager temporary tokens passed in the S3 bucket website redirect rules.
items.exp: CloudFront Signed Cookies are specifically designed for scenarios where you want to grant time-limited access to multiple restricted files (such as hundreds of HLS `.ts` video segments under a directory prefix) without changing the relative URLs inside manifest/playlist files.

items.q: A healthcare fintech partner submits loan applications through Mammoth Capital's web portal, which is fronted by Amazon CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer (ALB) routing to Node.js containers on ECS. The payload contains a JSON body where most fields (loan amount, term, zip code) are needed by the Node.js routing tier, but the applicant's Social Security Number (`ssn`) must be encrypted at the network edge so that even if someone dumps memory or logs on the ALB or Node.js tier, only the isolated back-office underwriting microservice holding a private RSA key can decrypt the `ssn` field. Which feature provides this without custom client-side encryption code?
opts: CloudFront Field-Level Encryption configured with the underwriting service's public key.
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) TLS 1.3 termination on the Application Load Balancer.
S3 Server-Side Encryption with KMS (SSE-KMS) on the ALB access logs bucket.
AWS WAF Regex Pattern Set rule with header redaction enabled.
items.exp: CloudFront Field-Level Encryption uses asymmetric encryption at the CloudFront edge location to encrypt specific POST form/JSON fields using a public key you upload, ensuring those fields remain ciphertext through the ALB and intermediate tiers until decrypted by the backend service holding the matching private key.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's security policy mandates that EC2 worker instances in private subnets may only make outbound HTTPS connections to three approved financial data domains (`*.sec.gov`, `*.nasdaq.com`, and `*.nyse.com`), and all outbound traffic must also be inspected against Suricata-compatible Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) signatures before reaching the NAT Gateway. Standard Security Groups and NACLs cannot filter by domain name or inspect packet signatures. Which managed AWS service meets both requirements?
opts: AWS Network Firewall deployed in a dedicated firewall subnet between the private subnets and the NAT Gateway.
Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall alone.
AWS WAF attached to the NAT Gateway.
Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring.
items.exp: AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful network firewall and intrusion detection/prevention service for VPCs that natively supports both outbound FQDN/domain allowlists (via SNI and HTTP Host headers) and Suricata-compatible IPS signature rules.

items.q: Mammoth Capital has 15 VPCs connected via an AWS Transit Gateway and needs to route all inter-VPC and internet-bound traffic through a fleet of third-party Palo Alto virtual network appliances running on EC2 in a central Inspection VPC. The architecture must scale the firewall appliances horizontally behind a load balancer, preserve the original source and destination IP addresses in the packets, and automatically bypass unhealthy appliances without complex BGP routing per VPC. Which AWS load balancer is purpose-built for this?
opts: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
Network Load Balancer (NLB)
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) with Gateway Load Balancer Endpoints (GWLBE)
Classic Load Balancer (CLB)
items.exp: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) operates at Layer 3 (Network layer) and uses GENEVE encapsulation on port 6081 to transparently insert, scale, and health-check third-party virtual network appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS) inline while preserving original packet headers.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's Threat Hunting team suspects that a legacy third-party binary running on two Linux EC2 instances in a private subnet is covertly exfiltrating proprietary order-book states inside malformed DNS and ICMP payloads. Standard VPC Flow Logs confirm unusual packet counts, but because Flow Logs only capture metadata (5-tuple headers), the analysts cannot see the actual packet payloads. They need to capture a real-time copy of the raw network packets entering and leaving those two EC2 instances' Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) and stream them to a Zeek/Suricata analysis appliance behind a Network Load Balancer without installing any agents on the suspect instances. Which AWS feature accomplishes this?
opts: Enable VPC Flow Logs with custom log formats v5 enriched with TCP flags and packet byte offsets.
Configure an Application Load Balancer access log stream to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Configure VPC Traffic Mirroring on the two suspect ENIs with a mirror filter and a mirror target pointing to the Network Load Balancer.
Enable AWS CloudTrail Data Events on `AWS::EC2::NetworkInterface` resources.
items.exp: VPC Traffic Mirroring copies raw network packets (including full Layer 2–7 payloads, truncated if desired) directly from Nitro-based EC2 Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) and encapsulates them in VXLAN (UDP port 4789) to a mirror target (such as an ENI, NLB, or GWLB endpoint) without requiring any host agent.

items.q: Mammoth Capital uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database with a primary cluster in `us-east-1` and a secondary cluster in `eu-west-1` to meet a 60-second recovery time objective (RTO). Their compliance policy mandates that the master database credentials be rotated automatically every 14 days without application downtime, and if `us-east-1` suffers a full regional outage, the failover application stack in `eu-west-1` must immediately read the current database password locally without making cross-Region calls back to `us-east-1`. Which solution meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?
opts: Store the database password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Standard tier in `us-east-1` and run a daily cron job on an EC2 instance to copy it to `eu-west-1`.
Hardcode the database credentials inside an encrypted AWS Lambda environment variable deployed in both Regions.
Store the password in an Amazon S3 bucket with Cross-Region Replication (CRR) enabled and write a custom Python script to run `ALTER USER` every 14 days.

Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager in `us-east-1`, enable automatic rotation using the managed Aurora rotation integration, and enable Secrets Manager multi-Region secret replication to `eu-west-1`.
items.exp: AWS Secrets Manager natively supports automatic credential rotation for Amazon Aurora and multi-Region secret replication. Whenever Secrets Manager rotates the secret in the primary Region (`us-east-1`), it automatically replicates the updated encrypted secret value to the replica secret in `eu-west-1`, ensuring local high-availability reads during a regional failover.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's internal microservices communicate over gRPC directly between EC2 instances and ECS tasks using private IP addresses and internal Route 53 private hosted zones (`*.internal.mammoth.local`). InfoSec mandates mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between every microservice using X.509 certificates signed by a dedicated, organization-owned Certificate Authority hierarchy. Because several microservices run inside custom sidecar proxies directly on the containers rather than behind an ALB or NLB, the team needs to export the private keys onto the containers upon startup. Which AWS service should they use to issue these certificates?
opts: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Public Certificates
AWS Secrets Manager Certificate Generator
AWS Private Certificate Authority (AWS Private CA)
AWS KMS Asymmetric RSA Signing Keys
items.exp: AWS Private Certificate Authority (AWS Private CA) lets you create a managed private CA hierarchy to issue private X.509 certificates for internal domains (`*.internal.mammoth.local`) and export certificates/private keys via the `IssueCertificate`/`GetCertificate` API or Private CA Connector for Kubernetes/containers to establish pod-to-pod mTLS.

items.q: At 03:15 UTC, an attacker exploits a deserialization flaw in a test web server in Mammoth Capital's staging VPC and begins querying Tor exit nodes and mining cryptocurrency. The Security Operations team wants an automated, serverless response pipeline that detects this anomalous behavior within minutes and immediately quarantines the compromised EC2 instance by replacing its Security Group with a zero-ingress/zero-egress `Forensic-Isolation-SG` and taking an EBS snapshot for investigation. Which architecture achieves this with the least custom engineering?
opts: Use AWS Trusted Advisor security checks polled every hour by a Jenkins server to modify the instance's Network ACL.
Configure Amazon Macie to monitor EC2 CPU utilization and trigger an AWS Batch job to terminate the instance.
Stream VPC Flow Logs to Amazon Redshift, run a scheduled SQL query every 6 hours, and send an email to the on-call engineer via Amazon SES.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty, create an Amazon EventBridge rule matching GuardDuty `CryptoCurrency:EC2/*` and `Trojan:EC2/*` findings, and trigger an AWS Lambda function (or SSM Automation runbook) that swaps the instance's Security Group and initiates EBS snapshots.
items.exp: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS query logs, and CloudTrail events using threat intelligence and ML to detect cryptocurrency mining, Tor C2 traffic, and Trojans. GuardDuty publishes findings in near real time to Amazon EventBridge, which can invoke an AWS Lambda function or Systems Manager Automation runbook to isolate the instance's Security Group and snapshot its volumes.

items.q: Mammoth Capital deploys Python and Go trading containers to Amazon ECR, runs serverless webhook handlers on AWS Lambda, and hosts matching engines on Amazon EC2. To satisfy their cyber-insurance underwriter, they must continuously scan all EC2 OS packages (without installing separate third-party agents beyond the standard SSM Agent), ECR container images (both on push and continuously as new CVEs are published), and Lambda function code/dependencies for software vulnerabilities, and feed prioritized risk scores into AWS Security Hub. Which AWS service provides this unified vulnerability scanning?
opts: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
AWS Artifact
items.exp: Amazon Inspector (v2) provides automated, continuous vulnerability management across Amazon EC2 (leveraging the existing AWS Systems Manager Agent rather than a standalone agent), Amazon ECR container images, and AWS Lambda functions (both package dependencies and code scanning), automatically routing CVE findings with contextual risk scores to AWS Security Hub.

items.q: Mammoth Capital has enabled Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, Amazon Macie, and AWS Security Hub across 30 AWS accounts. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this investigation?
opts: AWS Security Hub
Amazon CloudWatch Contributor Insights
Amazon Detective
AWS Audit Manager
items.exp: Amazon Detective automatically ingests time-series events from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, EKS audit logs, and GuardDuty findings, and uses machine learning and graph theory to build an interactive behavior graph for rapid root-cause security investigations and blast-radius visualization.

items.q: During a hasty migration of historical client onboarding documents from an on-premises NAS into 40 Amazon S3 buckets, an operations engineer accidentally mixed unredacted U.S. passport numbers, Social Security numbers, and credit card numbers into buckets meant for non-sensitive analytics. Mammoth Capital's Data Privacy Officer needs an automated service that uses machine learning and custom regex data identifiers to scan those 40 S3 buckets, inventory which objects contain PII or financial account numbers, and emit findings to Amazon EventBridge. Which AWS service should be used?
opts: Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty S3 Protection
AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon Macie

items.q: Despite training, developers in Mammoth Capital's R&D account occasionally modify Security Groups to allow `0.0.0.0/0` on TCP port 22 (SSH) while debugging test instances. The Security Architect wants a native AWS compliance mechanism that continuously evaluates every Security Group change, marks any Security Group with unrestricted port 22 as `NON_COMPLIANT`, and automatically revokes the offending ingress rule within 60 seconds without writing custom Lambda code. Which combination accomplishes this?
opts: Amazon Inspector with an AWS Step Functions state machine
AWS CloudTrail Insights paired with an Amazon SNS email notification
AWS Config with the `restricted-ssh` managed rule and an automatic remediation action using the `AWS-DisableIncomingSSHOnPort22` Systems Manager Automation runbook
AWS Trusted Advisor with an Amazon EventBridge schedule that runs every Sunday
items.exp: AWS Config continuously records resource configuration changes, evaluates them against the `restricted-ssh` (`INCOMING_SSH_DISABLED`) managed rule upon every change, and can trigger automatic remediation using prebuilt AWS Systems Manager Automation documents (such as `AWS-DisableIncomingSSHOnPort22` or `AWSConfigRemediation-RemoveUnrestrictedSourceIngressRules`) with zero custom code.

items.q: During a regulatory examination, an enforcement attorney challenges Mammoth Capital to mathematically prove that none of its AWS CloudTrail log files stored in an S3 archive bucket over the past 24 months were modified, backdated, or deleted after CloudTrail delivered them. Which native CloudTrail feature provides cryptographic proof that log files have remained unaltered (or reveals if any log file was deleted) since delivery?
opts: S3 Server-Side Encryption with AWS Managed Keys (SSE-S3)
CloudTrail Lake SQL query history logs
VPC Flow Log sequence numbering
CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation
items.exp: CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation generates hourly digest files containing SHA-256 hashes of every delivered log file and digitally signs each digest file using an RSA public/private key pair (chaining each digest to the previous hour's digest). Using `aws cloudtrail validate-logs`, auditors can mathematically verify that no log was modified or deleted after delivery.

items.q: Mammoth Capital runs 30 Python microservices on AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS that connect to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance (`db.m6g.xlarge`) handling average connection rates of 40 connections per second. The security team wants to eliminate all static database passwords for these microservices, enforce short-lived credentials that automatically expire after 15 minutes, and require encrypted SSL/TLS connections in transit. Which RDS feature satisfies these requirements?
opts: Enable RDS Multi-AZ with an active-active read replica.

Enable IAM Database Authentication on the RDS for PostgreSQL instance, grant the `rds-db:connect` action in the microservices' IAM roles, and configure the PostgreSQL database users with the `rds_iam` role and SSL enforcement.
Store a static password in an unencrypted S3 bucket and have the containers download it on startup.
Enable Kerberos authentication using an on-premises Active Directory domain controller over a public IP.
items.exp: RDS IAM Database Authentication works with MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL. Applications call `rds.generate_db_auth_token()` using their IAM task/execution role to generate a cryptographically signed authentication token valid for 15 minutes over SSL/TLS, completely eliminating static passwords for workloads well within the ~200 connections/sec threshold.

items.q: During a penetration test on a containerized chart-rendering service running on Amazon EC2, the red team discovered a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability that allowed them to trick the web application into sending a single HTTP `GET` request to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` and exfiltrating the EC2 instance profile's temporary IAM credentials. How should the engineer harden the EC2 fleet so that simple `GET` SSRF attacks cannot query instance metadata, and containers bridged via Docker's `docker0` network cannot reach the host's metadata service?
opts: Block `169.254.169.254` in the VPC Network ACL inbound and outbound rules.
Remove the IAM Instance Profile and store long-lived IAM User credentials in `/etc/environment` on the host.
Switch the EC2 instance from a private subnet to a public subnet with an Elastic IP.
Enforce Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) by setting `HttpTokens=required` and setting `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1` on the EC2 instances.
items.exp: IMDSv2 (`HttpTokens=required`) requires a session-oriented `PUT` request with a custom `X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds` header to obtain a secret token before any `GET` request can succeed, neutralizing classic `GET`-based SSRF attacks and open-proxy forwarding (`X-Forwarded-For` is rejected). Setting `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1` ensures the `PUT` response packet's IP TTL is 1, so it cannot cross the extra router hop of a bridged container network (`docker0`).

items.q: Mammoth Capital operates 55 AWS accounts inside an AWS Organization. New application teams frequently launch internet-facing Application Load Balancers (ALBs) and API Gateway endpoints across these accounts, sometimes forgetting to attach an AWS WAF Web ACL or enable AWS Shield Advanced protection. The CISO wants a single centralized service managed from a delegated security administrator account that automatically attaches a mandatory baseline AWS WAF Web ACL (blocking SQLi/XSS and Log4j exploits) and Shield Advanced protection to every existing and newly created ALB across all accounts in the Organization, even if an application developer tries to remove the Web ACL locally. Which service should the CISO use?
opts: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)
AWS Security Hub CSPM
AWS Firewall Manager
AWS Systems Manager State Manager
items.exp: AWS Firewall Manager integrates with AWS Organizations to centrally configure, deploy, and enforce AWS WAF rules, AWS Shield Advanced protections, Security Groups, AWS Network Firewall, and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall policies across all accounts and resources matching scope tags or resource types, automatically remediating non-compliant or newly created ALBs.

items.q: Mammoth Capital processes multi-party dark-pool trade orders where even a root administrator or compromised OS kernel on the host Amazon EC2 instance must not be able to inspect the plaintext order book in memory. The architecture requires carving out a cryptographically isolated compute environment from the parent Nitro-based EC2 instance with its own dedicated CPU cores and memory, no persistent storage, no interactive shell, and no external networking—communicating with the parent instance strictly over a local virtual socket (`vsock`). Additionally, AWS KMS must verify a signed cryptographic attestation document (`PCR0` image hash) before allowing the isolated environment to decrypt the order-book key. Which AWS technology provides this?
opts: AWS Dedicated Hosts (`mac2.metal`)
Amazon ECS with `awsvpc` network mode
AWS Lambda SnapStart
AWS Nitro Enclaves integrated with AWS KMS cryptographic attestation
items.exp: AWS Nitro Enclaves allow customers to carve out isolated CPU and memory partitions on a single Nitro-based EC2 instance with no persistent storage, no external networking (only a local `vsock` channel to the parent EC2 instance), and no administrator/root access. Nitro Enclaves integrate natively with AWS KMS (`kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384` / `PCR0`) so only a cryptographically attested enclave image can decrypt sensitive keys.

items.q: A derivatives clearinghouse subsidiary of Mammoth Capital is subject to a strict banking mandate requiring that all cryptographic signing keys for SWIFT wire transfers reside in dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-3 Level 3 Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) inside their own VPC, where Mammoth's security officers—not AWS—exclusively control the HSM quorum, user management, and key generation via standard PKCS#11 and Java Cryptography Extension (JCE) libraries, and where TLS termination can be offloaded directly from web servers to the HSM cluster. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
opts: AWS KMS with AWS Managed Keys
AWS Secrets Manager with Customer Managed Keys
AWS CloudHSM
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Advanced Tier
items.exp: AWS CloudHSM provisions dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated Hardware Security Module appliances inside your VPC. You retain full administrative control over the HSM partitions and quorum, and applications interact directly with the cluster over low-latency VPC ENIs using industry-standard PKCS#11, JCE, and OpenSSL/NGINX TLS offload engines.

items.q: A junior engineer at Mammoth Capital deployed a containerized order-settlement worker on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate. The container needs two distinct sets of permissions: (1) the ECS container agent must pull a private Docker image from Amazon ECR, fetch a database secret from AWS Secrets Manager at startup to inject as an environment variable, and push container stdout logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs; and (2) the Python code running inside the container must read and delete messages from an Amazon SQS queue (`settlement-jobs`). Following the principle of least privilege, how should these IAM permissions be separated in the ECS Task Definition?
opts: Attach both ECR/CloudWatch/Secrets Manager permissions and SQS permissions directly to the VPC NAT Gateway's IAM Role.
Put all permissions on the `executionRoleArn` (Task Execution Role) and leave `taskRoleArn` blank, because the container code automatically inherits the Task Execution Role.
Create an IAM User with long-lived access keys and bake `~/.aws/credentials` into the Docker image layer.

Assign the ECR, CloudWatch Logs, and startup Secrets Manager permissions to the ECS Task Execution Role (`executionRoleArn`), and assign the `sqs:ReceiveMessage` and `sqs:DeleteMessage` permissions to the ECS Task Role (`taskRoleArn`).
items.exp: In Amazon ECS, the Task Execution Role (`executionRoleArn`) grants the ECS infrastructure agent permissions to pull images from ECR, push stdout logs to CloudWatch Logs, and inject secrets from Secrets Manager/SSM at startup. The Task Role (`taskRoleArn`) grants the application code running inside the container temporary credentials to call AWS APIs like SQS, S3, or DynamoDB.

items.q: Mammoth Capital uses an Amazon DynamoDB Global Table replicated across `us-east-1` and `us-west-2` to store client session tokens encrypted on the client side using the AWS Encryption SDK before writing to DynamoDB. Previously, the application encrypted each item with a regional AWS KMS key in `us-east-1`, which meant during a failover to `us-west-2`, the `us-west-2` application servers still had to make cross-Region network calls back to the `us-east-1` KMS endpoint to decrypt the ciphertext—creating a single-Region dependency. Going forward, how can the architect make every ciphertext decryptable locally in `us-west-2` using the `us-west-2` KMS endpoint?
opts: Export the KMS key material from `us-east-1` as plaintext and store it in a public GitHub repository.
Disable KMS encryption and rely solely on Base64 encoding of the session tokens.
Create an AWS KMS Multi-Region Primary Key (`mrk-*`) in `us-east-1` and replicate it as a Multi-Region Replica Key into `us-west-2` so both Regions share the same key ID and cryptographic material.
Use an AWS CloudHSM cluster in `us-east-1` with a VPC Gateway Endpoint in `us-west-2`.
items.exp: AWS KMS Multi-Region keys (`mrk-*`) are sets of interoperable KMS keys in different AWS Regions that share the exact same key ID (`mrk-...`) and cryptographic key material. Ciphertext encrypted with a Multi-Region key in `us-east-1` can be decrypted locally in `us-west-2` using the local replica key with zero cross-Region network calls. An existing single-Region key cannot be converted into a Multi-Region key, so items encrypted under the old key must be re-encrypted once under the new Multi-Region key.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's Threat Intelligence team maintains a dynamic blocklist of 15,000 malicious command-and-control (C2) and phishing domains. They want to block all EC2 instances, ECS tasks, and Lambda functions across 40 VPCs in their AWS Organization from resolving those domains whenever workloads query the VPC-native Amazon Route 53 Resolver (`169.254.169.253` / `.2` address), while returning a custom `NXDOMAIN` response and logging blocked queries to Amazon CloudWatch Logs—without deploying inline NAT or firewall appliances in every VPC. Which solution meets these requirements?
opts: Configure VPC Network ACLs in all 40 VPCs to block UDP port 53 to `169.254.169.253`.
Create 40 public Route 53 Hosted Zones with alias records pointing to `127.0.0.1`.
Deploy AWS WAF on the VPC Internet Gateways with a Geographic Match rule.

Create a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group containing the blocked domain list, share it across the Organization using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) or AWS Firewall Manager, and associate it with the 40 VPCs.
items.exp: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall lets you filter and regulate outbound DNS queries made through the VPC Route 53 Resolver against managed or custom domain lists ( returning `NXDOMAIN`, `NODATA`, or a custom IP override), and rule groups can be shared across accounts via AWS RAM and centrally enforced via AWS Firewall Manager.

items.q: Mammoth Capital currently spends $85,000/month on On-Demand compute across `us-east-1` and `eu-west-1`. Their engineering roadmap for the next 12 months includes migrating 40% of their `c6i` EC2 Linux instances in `us-east-1` to `c7g` Graviton instances, moving three batch microservices from EC2 to AWS Fargate in `eu-west-1`, and refactoring a webhook tier onto AWS Lambda. Which pricing model should the architect recommend?
