SNS can only send SMS text messages, whereas SQS can only send emails.
Both SNS and SQS require all subscribers to run inside the same Availability Zone.
items.exp: SNS is push-based—it actively pushes messages to subscribers the moment they are published (so offline direct endpoints miss them)—whereas SQS is pull-based and durably retains messages for up to 14 days until polled.

items.q: When a new client signs up at Mammoth Capital, one event needs to simultaneously send a welcome email, invoke an onboarding Lambda, push a record to an analytics SQS queue, call a CRM HTTP webhook, and send an SMS to the sales desk. Which AWS service broadcasts one message to all five subscriber types at once?
opts: Amazon SQS Standard Queue
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
AWS Step Functions Express Workflow
Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service)
items.exp: Amazon SNS is a managed pub/sub service where publishing one message to an SNS Topic immediately delivers copies to all subscribed SQS queues, Lambda functions, HTTP/HTTPS webhooks, emails, and SMS numbers.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's trade fulfillment pipeline needs to run a long, auditable process that can take several days (including a human-approval step), must execute each step never more than once, and is billed per state transition. Which Step Functions workflow type fits?
opts: Standard Workflows, which run for up to a year, execute each step exactly once, and charge per state transition.
Express Workflows, which cap execution at 5 minutes and execute at-least-once.
Chaining four Lambda functions manually with hardcoded retry loops in application code.
An Amazon SNS Topic broadcasting to all steps simultaneously.
items.exp: Step Functions Standard Workflows support executions lasting up to 1 year with exactly-once step execution and a full visual audit history, built for long-running processes like order fulfillment and human approvals.

items.q: Mammoth Capital ingests thousands of high-volume streaming telemetry events per second. Each event triggers a short workflow that finishes in under 5 minutes, and every step is written to be idempotent. Which Step Functions option is designed for this high-throughput workload?
opts: Standard Workflows (up to 1 year duration, priced per state transition)
SQS Dead Letter Queues with 14-day retention
A single Lambda function with a 60-minute timeout
Express Workflows (up to 5 minutes duration, at-least-once execution, priced by duration and requests)
items.exp: Step Functions Express Workflows are built for high-volume, short-duration (up to 5 minutes) event processing such as IoT ingestion or streaming transformations, executing at-least-once and billing by duration and request count.

items.q: An order pipeline must charge a card, reserve inventory, arrange shipping, and—if shipping fails—automatically roll back the inventory hold while showing engineers a live visual diagram of which step failed at 2 AM. Why should you use AWS Step Functions here instead of SQS or SNS?
opts: Because SQS and SNS cannot trigger Lambda functions in AWS.
Because Step Functions replaces RDS and DynamoDB as the primary database for inventory data.

Because SQS and SNS decouple independent services without tracking the overall workflow, whereas Step Functions orchestrates a defined sequence with branching, exponential-backoff retries, rollbacks, and visual state tracking.
Because Step Functions allows a single Lambda function to run for 12 hours without timing out.
items.exp: While SQS and SNS decouple services that shouldn't know about each other, Step Functions acts as the central conductor of a multi-step state machine with sequencing, parallel branches, retries, catch/rollback logic, and a live visual audit trail.

items.q: Mammoth Capital exposes a market-analytics REST API via Amazon API Gateway backed by AWS Lambda and RDS. Thousands of clients query the exact same end-of-day summary endpoint every minute, driving up Lambda invocation and database costs. What is the simplest way to reduce backend load?
opts: Switch from a REST API to a WebSocket API
Enable API Gateway stage caching with an appropriate TTL
Increase the API Gateway integration timeout beyond 29 seconds
Replace IAM Authorization with API Keys
items.exp: API Gateway REST APIs support built-in response caching with configurable TTLs (up to 3,600s), returning cached responses directly from the gateway without invoking Lambda or querying RDS.
items.topic: API Gateway: The Serverless Front Door

items.q: A client uploads a trade reconciliation file through Amazon API Gateway to a synchronous AWS Lambda function that takes 90 seconds to parse and validate. Although the Lambda timeout is set to 5 minutes, the client consistently receives a 504 Gateway Timeout after 29 seconds. How should the architect fix this?
opts: Have API Gateway enqueue the request directly into Amazon SQS, return a 202 status code immediately, and let Lambda process the queue asynchronously
Provision 10 GB of memory on the Lambda function and enable Provisioned Concurrency
Place a Network Load Balancer in front of API Gateway to keep the TCP socket open for 5 minutes
Attach an AWS WAF Web ACL to buffer the HTTP request
items.exp: API Gateway has a default 29-second integration timeout. Decoupling synchronous long-running work by integrating API Gateway with SQS (or async invocation) returns an immediate acknowledgement while Lambda processes the job in the background.
items.topic: API Gateway: The Serverless Front Door

items.q: An engineering team needs to authenticate external partner requests at API Gateway using custom bearer tokens issued by an existing on-premises identity provider that is not SAML or OIDC compliant. Which API Gateway feature should they configure?
opts: API Keys with a Usage Plan
IAM Authorization with SigV4
A Gateway VPC Endpoint
A Lambda Authorizer
items.exp: A Lambda Authorizer uses a custom Lambda function to validate proprietary or third-party bearer tokens and returns an IAM policy document granting or denying access.
items.topic: API Gateway: The Serverless Front Door

items.q: Mammoth Capital integrates with a third-party SaaS compliance platform (Datadog/Zendesk) and wants events generated in the SaaS platform to trigger AWS Step Functions workflows without provisioning EC2 instances or managing public webhook URLs. Which service provides native SaaS partner integration?
opts: Amazon SQS FIFO Queue
Amazon SNS Topic
Amazon EventBridge Partner Event Bus
AWS PrivateLink Interface Endpoint
items.exp: Amazon EventBridge Partner Event Buses receive events directly from supported SaaS partners without requiring custom webhook infrastructure or API Gateways.

items.q: A settlement microservice at Mammoth Capital had a logic bug in production for 2 hours, causing it to miscalculate fees on incoming trade events. After deploying a hotfix, the team needs to reprocess only the trade events from that 2-hour window without asking upstream systems to re-emit them. Which feature solves this?
opts: EventBridge Event Archive and Replay
SNS Message Filtering with Delivery Retries
SQS Visibility Timeout extension
CloudTrail Event History export
items.exp: EventBridge Archive captures events matching a filter pattern for a defined retention period, and Replay lets you re-inject events from a specific start/end timestamp window back into the event bus.

items.q: An operations engineer wants to automatically invoke an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to isolate an EC2 instance whenever Amazon GuardDuty generates a finding with a severity score greater than 7.0. What is the simplest serverless way to wire this up?
opts: Poll the GuardDuty API every minute from a cron job on an EC2 instance
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule on the Default Event Bus matching GuardDuty findings with severity > 7.0 and set Systems Manager as the target
Stream CloudTrail logs through Kinesis Data Firehose to S3 and query with Athena
Attach an SQS Dead Letter Queue directly to GuardDuty
items.exp: AWS services like GuardDuty emit findings automatically to the Default Event Bus in EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can filter on the JSON severity field and trigger remediation targets like Systems Manager or Lambda in near real-time.

items.q: Mammoth Capital wants to run code to process Bitcoin transactions triggered by an S3 upload, without managing any servers. Which service is appropriate?
opts: ECS
EKS
Fargate
Lambda
items.exp: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events (like S3 uploads) without provisioning or managing servers.

items.q: Which service allows Mammoth to coordinate multiple Lambda functions into a visual workflow for their complex trade settlement process?
opts: SQS
SNS
Step Functions
EventBridge
items.exp: AWS Step Functions provides serverless orchestration for modern applications, allowing you to build visual workflows linking Lambda functions and other services.

items.q: Mammoth needs a fully managed, serverless, GraphQL API layer for their new client portal. Which service should they choose?
opts: API Gateway
AppSync
Cognito
Amplify
items.exp: AWS AppSync is a fully managed serverless GraphQL API service. API Gateway is typically used for REST or WebSocket APIs.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's web app is hosted in us-east-1, and users in Sydney experience 200+ ms latency loading HTML, CSS, JS, and images from S3. The security team also requires that users can never bypass the CDN to access the S3 bucket directly. What should the architect configure?
opts: AWS Global Accelerator in front of the S3 bucket to cache static images at two anycast IPs.
Make the S3 bucket public and route Sydney users through a Bastion Host.
An Amazon CloudFront distribution caching assets at hundreds of edge locations, paired with Origin Access Control (OAC) restricting S3 access to CloudFront only.
An Application Load Balancer in us-east-1 with no edge layer.
items.exp: Amazon CloudFront caches static HTTP/HTTPS content at edge locations worldwide (so Sydney users are served from Sydney), while Origin Access Control (OAC) ensures users cannot bypass CloudFront to read the S3 bucket directly.

items.q: Mammoth Capital runs a real-time TCP/UDP trading and gaming feed across multiple Regions where payloads cannot be cached. They need two static anycast IP addresses for client firewall whitelisting, sub-30-second regional failover, and routing over AWS's private global backbone instead of the congested public internet. Which service should they choose?
opts: AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon CloudFront with 24-hour Cache Behaviors
S3 Origin Access Control (OAC)
Route 53 Simple Routing
items.exp: AWS Global Accelerator does not cache content; it provides two static anycast IP addresses, routes TCP/UDP traffic from the nearest edge over AWS's private backbone, and fails over between Regions in under 30 seconds.

items.q: Within a single CloudFront distribution, how do you configure CloudFront to cache /static/* files for 24 hours while forwarding /api/* requests directly to an Application Load Balancer with no caching?
opts: Create two separate VPCs and connect them with VPC Peering.
Define URL pattern rules using CloudFront Cache Behaviors.
Attach an Origin Access Control (OAC) policy directly to the ALB's TCP port.
Switch the CloudFront distribution from HTTP/HTTPS to UDP.
items.exp: CloudFront Cache Behaviors let you map URL path patterns like /static/* and /api/* to specific cache settings and origins within the same distribution.

items.q: In Mammoth Capital's network, VPC-A is peered with VPC-B, and VPC-B is peered with VPC-C. An engineer in VPC-A tries to reach a database in VPC-C expecting traffic to route through VPC-B, but the connection fails. Why?
opts: VPC Peering routes traffic over the public internet and requires an Internet Gateway in all three VPCs.
VPC Peering only supports IPv6 traffic when more than two VPCs exist.
VPC Peering requires an hourly attachment fee to be paid on VPC-B first.
VPC Peering is non-transitive; VPC-A cannot reach VPC-C through VPC-B without a direct VPC-A-to-VPC-C peering connection or an AWS Transit Gateway.
items.exp: VPC Peering is strictly 1-to-1 and non-transitive—traffic from VPC-A cannot hop through VPC-B to reach VPC-C.

items.q: Mammoth Capital has scaled to 50 VPCs across production, staging, and shared services, plus on-premises VPN connections. Full-mesh VPC Peering would require 1,225 separate peering connections. What should the architect deploy instead?
opts: A NAT Gateway in every VPC routing traffic over the public internet.
An AWS Transit Gateway as a centralized regional hub-and-spoke router, requiring just 50 connections (one per VPC) and a central route table.
A single S3 Gateway Endpoint shared across all 50 VPCs.
Bastion Hosts chained across all 50 VPCs.
items.exp: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub-and-spoke router: each of the 50 VPCs connects once to the Transit Gateway (50 attachments instead of 1,225 peering links), which also supports VPN, Direct Connect Gateway, and inter-region peering.

items.q: A small homelab-style test project in AWS has just two VPCs in the same Region that need private backbone connectivity at the lowest possible cost. Why is VPC Peering preferred over Transit Gateway for this simple setup?
opts: VPC Peering has no hourly attachment charge (you only pay for data transfer), whereas Transit Gateway charges per attachment-hour and per GB of data processed.
Transit Gateway cannot route traffic between fewer than 10 VPCs.
VPC Peering automatically caches static web assets at edge PoPs.
Transit Gateway traverses the public internet whereas VPC Peering uses the AWS backbone.
items.exp: For connecting just 2 or 3 VPCs without complex transitive routing, VPC Peering is simpler and free of hourly attachment fees (charging only for data transfer), whereas Transit Gateway charges per attachment-hour and per GB processed.

items.q: Mammoth Capital streams about 800 Mbps of real-time market data from its Chicago data center to VPCs in us-east-1. They require consistent sub-5ms network jitter that bypasses the public internet, AND strict financial regulations require all packets in transit to be encrypted with IPsec. Which architecture meets these requirements?
opts: A single AWS Direct Connect 10 Gbps connection with a Private VIF only
An AWS Direct Connect 10 Gbps connection with an AWS Site-to-Site VPN configured over it
Two AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections over the public internet using Accelerated VPN
VPC Peering between the Chicago data center and us-east-1
items.exp: Direct Connect provides the dedicated private fiber for consistent latency and bandwidth, while running an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over Direct Connect adds the required IPsec encryption (since DX is unencrypted by default).
items.topic: Hybrid Connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect

items.q: A company already uses a single AWS Direct Connect connection between its corporate headquarters and an AWS Transit Gateway. The CIO wants to eliminate the single point of failure of the Direct Connect circuit using the most cost-effective backup connection possible. What should the architect recommend?
opts: Order a second Dedicated Direct Connect connection at a second colocation facility
Enable Cross-Zone Load Balancing on the Direct Connect Gateway
Replace the Direct Connect connection with an AWS Snowball Edge device
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the Transit Gateway and configure BGP routing to use it as a backup path
items.exp: A second Direct Connect circuit is the most resilient option, but when the requirement specifies 'most cost-effective backup,' an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet with BGP failover provides automatic backup without paying for a second physical fiber port.
items.topic: Hybrid Connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect

items.q: An enterprise has a single AWS Direct Connect connection terminating in Northern Virginia, and needs to route private traffic from on-premises to 15 VPCs spread across three different AWS Regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, and eu-west-1). Which combination accomplishes this?
opts: Create a Direct Connect Gateway connected to a Transit Gateway in each of the three Regions over a Transit VIF
Attach a Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) from all 15 VPCs directly to the single Private VIF without a Direct Connect Gateway
Use VPC Gateway Endpoints in each Region
Enable Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN on the Customer Gateway
items.exp: A Direct Connect Gateway (DXGW) is a global resource that bridges a Direct Connect connection (via a Transit VIF) to multiple Transit Gateways in different AWS Regions.
items.topic: Hybrid Connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect

items.q: Which service should Mammoth Capital use to monitor the CPU utilization of their EC2 instances in real-time?
opts: CloudTrail
CloudWatch
Config
Systems Manager
items.exp: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service that collects operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events (like CPU utilization).

items.q: Mammoth's CISO needs an audit trail of every API call made in the AWS account, including who made it and when. Which service provides this?
opts: CloudWatch
CloudTrail
Inspector
GuardDuty
items.exp: AWS CloudTrail tracks user activity and API usage, providing a complete audit trail for compliance and security analysis.

items.q: To automate the patching of thousands of EC2 instances across their environment, Mammoth should use:
opts: CloudFormation
OpsWorks
Systems Manager Patch Manager
CodeDeploy
items.exp: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates the process of patching managed instances with both security related and other types of updates.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's compliance auditors mandate that for all encrypted S3 buckets, RDS databases, and EBS volumes, Mammoth Capital—not AWS—must own the encryption key policy, control who can use the key, and record every Encrypt and Decrypt API call in CloudTrail. Which KMS key option satisfies this?
opts: AWS Managed Keys (such as aws/s3 and aws/rds), because they are free and rotate annually.
Customer Managed Keys (CMKs), where you own the key policy, control rotation, and get full CloudTrail audit logs of key usage.
Unencrypted EBS Snapshots paired with an S3 Bucket Policy.
Public SSL/TLS certificates from ACM.
items.exp: AWS maintains administrative access to AWS Managed Keys (aws/s3, aws/rds), so strict compliance requirements mandating customer control over key policies and rotation schedules require Customer Managed Keys (CMKs).

items.q: When Mammoth Capital encrypts a 5 GB object in S3 using KMS, how does AWS avoid the slow and expensive process of sending the entire 5 GB file over the network to the KMS service?
opts: KMS compresses the 5 GB object down to 1 KB using lossy compression before encrypting it.
KMS only encrypts the S3 bucket name and leaves the 5 GB file in plaintext.
Envelope Encryption: KMS generates a Data Key that encrypts the 5 GB object locally at high speed, and your CMK in KMS encrypts only that tiny Data Key.
KMS requires shipping a physical Snowcone device for any object over 1 GB.
items.exp: Through Envelope Encryption, your 5 GB object never travels to KMS; instead, KMS generates a Data Key to encrypt the object locally, and your CMK encrypts and secures only the tiny Data Key.

items.q: For an internal sandbox account with no strict audit rules, an engineer uses AWS Managed Keys (aws/s3 and aws/rds) instead of creating Customer Managed Keys (CMKs). How do AWS Managed Keys compare to CMKs in price and rotation?
opts: AWS Managed Keys cost $100/month and never rotate, whereas CMKs are free.
AWS Managed Keys require manual rotation every 30 days by the root user.
AWS Managed Keys allow custom cross-account key policies, whereas CMKs do not.
AWS Managed Keys are free and automatically rotate every year, whereas CMKs cost ~$1/month per key (plus $0.03 per 10,000 API calls) in exchange for full customer control.
items.exp: AWS Managed Keys are free and rotated automatically by AWS once a year, while Customer Managed Keys cost ~$1/month per key plus per-API-call fees in exchange for customizable key policies and rotation control.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's public trading portal (fronted by an ALB and CloudFront) is being hit with credential-stuffing login floods from specific IPs and HTTP requests containing SQL injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payloads. Which service inspects Layer 7 request content to block these attacks?
opts: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) attached to the ALB, API Gateway, or CloudFront distribution
Amazon Macie scanning S3 buckets
AWS Shield Standard operating at Layers 3 and 4
KMS Envelope Encryption
items.exp: AWS WAF operates at Layer 7 (application layer), inspecting HTTP/HTTPS requests on an ALB, API Gateway, or CloudFront distribution to filter SQL injection, block XSS payloads, geo-block countries, and rate-limit IPs.

items.q: Every AWS customer automatically gets free protection against common Layer 3/4 SYN floods and UDP floods via AWS Shield Standard. Why would a financial firm like Mammoth Capital pay $3,000/month per organization for AWS Shield Advanced?
opts: Because Shield Standard is disabled by default unless you purchase Shield Advanced.
Because Shield Advanced scans S3 buckets for unencrypted Social Security Numbers and credit cards.

Because Shield Advanced adds protection against larger, sophisticated DDoS attacks, 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), real-time CloudWatch attack visibility, and financial protection against DDoS-induced scaling bills.
Because Shield Advanced replaces IAM Roles with temporary STS credentials.
items.exp: While Shield Standard is free and automatic for basic Layer 3/4 DDoS mitigation, Shield Advanced ($3,000/month) provides 24/7 DDoS Response Team (DRT) access, real-time CloudWatch visibility, and cost protection against DDoS scaling spikes.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's CISO wants an automated service that uses machine learning to scan all of the firm's S3 buckets and alert security if anyone accidentally uploaded CSVs containing client credit card numbers, Social Security Numbers, passport details, or API keys. Which service does this?
opts: AWS WAF
Amazon Macie
AWS Shield Standard
AWS Certificate Manager
items.exp: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to scan S3 buckets and automatically detect sensitive PII—such as credit card numbers, SSNs, passports, and API keys—sitting in unencrypted or exposed buckets.

items.q: Mammoth Capital needs a free place to store application feature flags, dev vs. prod database endpoint URLs, and KMS-encrypted configuration strings that do not require automatic rotation. Which service and option should they use?
opts: AWS Secrets Manager at $0.40 per secret per month
Hardcoding the values into EC2 user data in plaintext
AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Parameter Store using free Standard tier and KMS-encrypted SecureString parameters
AWS Security Token Service (STS)
items.exp: SSM Parameter Store's Standard tier is free and supports SecureString parameters encrypted at rest with KMS, making it ideal for feature flags, config settings, and secrets that don't need automated rotation.
items.topic: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store & AWS STS

items.q: To meet strict PCI-DSS and HIPAA compliance mandates, Mammoth Capital's RDS database passwords must automatically rotate every 30 days with zero application downtime while Lambda functions fetch the current password at runtime via GetSecretValue. Which service is required?
opts: SSM Parameter Store Standard tier
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
Amazon Macie
AWS Secrets Manager ($0.40/secret/month) with native automatic rotation
items.exp: AWS Secrets Manager natively integrates with RDS, Redshift, and DocumentDB to automatically rotate credentials on a schedule while applications call GetSecretValue at runtime with zero downtime.
items.topic: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store & AWS STS

items.q: When a Lambda function assumes an IAM Role, an EC2 instance uses an instance profile, or Account A accesses Account B's resources, which AWS service operates under the hood to vend temporary credentials (Access Key ID, Secret Key, and Session Token) with automatic expiry?
opts: AWS STS (Security Token Service)
AWS Secrets Manager
SSM Parameter Store
AWS WAF
items.exp: AWS Security Token Service (STS) powers IAM Roles, federated identity, and cross-account access by issuing short-lived temporary security credentials that expire automatically.
items.topic: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store & AWS STS

items.q: A developer sets up an EC2 instance running Apache directly on a public IP with no Load Balancer or CloudFront in front of it. Why can't they use a free public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) alone to enable HTTPS directly on that EC2 instance's OS?
opts: Public ACM certificates only encrypt S3 buckets at rest, not HTTPS traffic.
Public ACM certificates only attach to integrated services like Elastic Load Balancers (ALB/NLB), CloudFront, and API Gateway—they cannot be exported or installed directly onto an EC2 instance's OS.
ACM charges $3,000/month per public certificate unless attached to a NAT Gateway.
ACM only supports email validation, which Apache does not recognize.
items.exp: Free public ACM certificates integrate directly with ALB/NLB, CloudFront, and API Gateway, and cannot be exported or installed onto an individual EC2 instance's operating system (which would require a manually managed cert or paid ACM Private CA).
items.topic: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): Encryption in Transit

items.q: Mammoth Capital wants its free public SSL/TLS certificates in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to renew automatically without risking an outage because someone forgot to click a renewal link in an inbox. Which domain validation method should they use?
opts: DNS validation (adding the CNAME record ACM provides), which enables fully automatic renewal as long as the certificate is attached to a resource.
Email validation, which requires a human to click an approval link every renewal cycle.
KMS Envelope validation, which rotates the EBS volume key every 30 days.
Bastion Host SSH validation.
items.exp: DNS validation lets ACM verify the CNAME record in DNS automatically and renew attached certificates hands-free, whereas email validation requires someone to manually click a link every renewal cycle.
items.topic: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): Encryption in Transit

items.q: During an audit, an engineer states that encrypting all EBS volumes and S3 buckets with AWS KMS satisfies the requirement to protect customer data moving between browsers and the Application Load Balancer. Why is that statement wrong?
opts: Neither KMS nor ACM encrypts data; only AWS Shield encrypts traffic.
KMS only encrypts network traffic in transit, so the disks are actually unencrypted.
KMS encrypts data sitting at rest on storage, whereas protecting data moving in transit over the network requires an SSL/TLS certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) on the Load Balancer.
KMS automatically provisions HTTPS certificates in the browser, so no Load Balancer certificate is needed.
items.exp: KMS protects data at rest on disk, while AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and renews the SSL/TLS certificates that encrypt data in transit between users and your ALB, CloudFront, or API Gateway.
items.topic: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): Encryption in Transit

items.q: Mammoth Capital's Production Account stores financial statements in an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS using the default AWS Managed Key (aws/s3). An IAM Role in the Audit Account is granted s3:GetObject in both the S3 Bucket Policy and its IAM Role Policy, yet every download fails with Access Denied. Why?
opts: S3 Block Public Access is blocking the cross-account IAM Role

AWS Managed Keys (aws/s3) have read-only key policies that cannot be shared across accounts; Mammoth must re-encrypt the objects with a Customer Managed Key (CMK) and grant kms:Decrypt to the Audit Account
Cross-account S3 access requires SSE-C instead of SSE-KMS
S3 Bucket Keys must be disabled before cross-account reads can succeed
items.exp: You cannot modify the key policy of an AWS Managed Key (aws/s3) to grant cross-account permissions. Cross-account SSE-KMS requires a Customer Managed Key (CMK) whose key policy grants the external account kms:Decrypt, paired with kms:Decrypt on the external IAM role.

items.q: A high-throughput analytics application writes 50,000 objects per second to an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS. The team is hitting AWS KMS request-rate throttling limits and seeing a massive spike in monthly KMS API charges. What is the simplest way to resolve both issues while keeping SSE-KMS?
opts: Enable S3 Bucket Keys on the S3 bucket
Switch the bucket to Dual-Layer Server-Side Encryption (DSSE-KMS)
Create 50 separate KMS Customer Managed Keys and shard requests across them
Deploy an RDS Proxy in front of AWS KMS
items.exp: S3 Bucket Keys generate a short-lived bucket-level key within S3 from your KMS key, reducing request traffic from S3 to KMS (and the associated KMS API charges) by up to 99%.

items.q: Financial regulators require Mammoth Capital to retain trade confirmations in Amazon S3 for 7 years in a Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) state such that no user — including the AWS account root user — can delete, overwrite, or shorten the retention period. What should they configure?
opts: S3 Object Lock in Governance Mode with MFA Delete
An S3 Bucket Policy with an explicit Deny on s3:DeleteObject for all IAM users
S3 Versioning with a Lifecycle Policy transitioning objects to S3 Standard-IA
S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a 7-year retention period
items.exp: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode enforces strict WORM protection where no principal — not even the root user — can overwrite or delete an object version or shorten its retention period until it expires.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's DevSecOps team wants every Docker container image pushed to Amazon ECR and every AWS Lambda function deployment to be automatically scanned for known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure. Which service provides this continuously?
opts: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
Amazon Detective
Amazon Macie
items.exp: Amazon Inspector automatically discovers and continuously scans EC2 instances (via the SSM Agent), container images in Amazon ECR, and AWS Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure.
items.topic: Threat Detection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, Detective

items.q: After Amazon GuardDuty alerts Mammoth Capital's security team about unusual API calls coming from an IAM role, the incident response team needs to quickly visualize related VPC network traffic, geolocations, and correlated API calls over time using an interactive graph to determine the root cause. Which service is built for this investigation?
opts: Amazon Detective
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
AWS Shield Advanced
items.exp: Amazon Detective automatically collects log data from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty and uses machine learning and graph theory to build interactive visualizations for root-cause security investigations.
items.topic: Threat Detection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, Detective

items.q: A financial firm operates 40 AWS accounts and uses GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie. The CISO needs a single dashboard that aggregates findings from all three services across all accounts and continuously evaluates the environment against PCI-DSS and CIS AWS Foundations standards. Which service should they enable?
opts: AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Detective
AWS Security Hub
AWS Systems Manager Explorer
items.exp: AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings in the AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF) from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and partner tools while running automated compliance checks against standards like PCI-DSS and CIS.
items.topic: Threat Detection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, Detective

items.q: Mammoth Capital's iOS app allows retail customers to sign in with Google or Apple IDs and then upload tax documents directly from their phone into a dedicated per-user folder inside an Amazon S3 bucket without passing through EC2 or Lambda. Which architecture provides the temporary AWS credentials required for the S3 upload?
opts: AWS IAM Identity Center with Permission Sets
Amazon Cognito User Pool paired with a Cognito Identity Pool
Hardcoding an IAM User's access keys inside the iOS application binary
An AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString
items.exp: Cognito User Pools handle authentication and social federation (returning a JWT), while Cognito Identity Pools exchange that token via STS for temporary, fine-grained IAM credentials that allow the mobile app to upload directly to S3.
items.topic: App vs Workforce Identity: Cognito vs IAM Identity Center

items.q: A financial services company manages 75 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Their 400 engineers already authenticate against an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory and Okta. What is the recommended way to grant these engineers role-based, temporary CLI and console access across all 75 AWS accounts with minimal operational overhead?
opts: Create IAM Users in all 75 accounts and synchronize passwords with a Lambda script
Configure Amazon Cognito Identity Pools in each of the 75 accounts
Enable AWS IAM Identity Center integrated with Okta via SAML 2.0/SCIM and assign Permission Sets to groups across accounts
Share the Organization Management Account root credentials using AWS Secrets Manager
items.exp: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) centrally manages workforce access across multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations, federating with external IdPs like Okta or Active Directory and using Permission Sets to issue temporary STS credentials.
items.topic: App vs Workforce Identity: Cognito vs IAM Identity Center

items.q: A web application uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The development team wants a fully managed user directory with built-in sign-up, sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and native JWT validation at API Gateway without writing custom authentication code. Which service should they choose?
opts: Amazon Cognito User Pools
Amazon Cognito Identity Pools only
AWS IAM Identity Center
AWS Directory Service Simple AD
items.exp: Cognito User Pools provide a managed user directory with sign-up, sign-in, MFA, and native JWT authorizer integration with Amazon API Gateway and Application Load Balancers.

items.q: Which intelligent threat detection service uses machine learning to identify malicious activity, like a compromised EC2 instance mining Bitcoin?
opts: GuardDuty
Shield
WAF
Macie
items.exp: Amazon GuardDuty is a continuous security monitoring service that uses machine learning and threat intelligence to identify unexpected and potentially unauthorized activity.

items.q: Mammoth Capital needs to protect their web applications from common web exploits like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). Which service is designed for this?
opts: Network ACL
Security Group
AWS WAF
AWS Shield Standard
items.exp: AWS Web Application Firewall (WAF) helps protect web applications from common web exploits that could affect application availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources.

items.q: Which service automatically discovers, classifies, and protects sensitive data, such as PII in Mammoth's S3 buckets?
opts: KMS
Secrets Manager
Macie
Inspector
items.exp: Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data in AWS.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's central security team attaches a Service Control Policy (SCP) to an Organizational Unit (OU) that states "Deny all actions unless the region is us-east-1." A developer logs into a member account in that OU using the member account's Root User (and an IAM user with AdministratorAccess) and tries to launch an EC2 instance in eu-central-1. What happens?
opts: Both succeed because AdministratorAccess and the member account Root User override all SCPs.
The IAM user is blocked, but the member account Root User succeeds.
The instance launches, and AWS Config deletes it 24 hours later.
Both are denied; an SCP overrides everything in a member account, including local IAM Administrator policies and even the member account's Root User.
items.exp: In AWS Organizations, a Service Control Policy (SCP) defines the maximum permission boundary for member accounts and overrides all local IAM policies—even the root user of a member account cannot bypass an SCP denial.

items.q: A cloud administrator attaches an SCP with an Allow statement for EC2 to an Organizational Unit, expecting every new IAM user in those member accounts to immediately be able to launch EC2 instances without attaching any IAM policies to the users. Why are the users still denied?
opts: SCPs only apply after restarting the AWS Control Tower management console.
SCPs do not grant permissions; they act only as permission boundaries defining the maximum permissions that local IAM policies in the account can grant.
SCPs only work on single standalone accounts outside AWS Organizations.
EC2 does not support AWS Organizations.
items.exp: Service Control Policies (SCPs) never grant access by themselves—they only restrict the maximum permissions available in an account, so IAM entities still require local IAM policies to grant access.

items.q: Mammoth Capital wants to adopt a 50-account enterprise strategy for blast-radius isolation, complete with automated multi-account setup, pre-configured SCP guardrails, centralized logging into a dedicated Log Archive account, and automated CloudTrail across all accounts without building it from scratch. Which service provides this turnkey governance layer?
opts: AWS X-Ray
Amazon Athena
AWS Control Tower
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
items.exp: AWS Control Tower is the higher-level turnkey service built on AWS Organizations that automates setting up and governing a multi-account environment with pre-configured guardrails (SCPs), centralized CloudTrail, and a dedicated Log Archive account.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's trading algorithms generate 50,000 price ticks per minute. Three separate consumers—a Lambda function, an EC2 risk application, and Kinesis Data Analytics—need to read from the same real-time stream simultaneously at their own positions, with records retained for up to 365 days for replay. Which service should ingest this data?
opts: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
Amazon Athena
An RDS PostgreSQL database receiving 50,000 direct SQL INSERTs per minute
items.exp: Kinesis Data Streams uses parallel shards to ingest high-velocity real-time streams that multiple independent consumers can read simultaneously at their own position, retaining records for 24 hours by default and up to 365 days.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's infrastructure streams 10 GB of application logs per hour. The team doesn't need custom stream-processing code or multi-consumer replay—they just want a fully managed delivery pipe that buffers (minimum 60 seconds), batches, compresses, and loads the streaming data directly into S3 or Redshift. Which service fits?
opts: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with custom shard polling
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
Amazon Athena
AWS Control Tower
items.exp: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed delivery service that automatically buffers, batches, compresses, and loads streaming data directly into S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch with zero custom code.

items.q: Kinesis Data Firehose has been dumping JSON log files into an S3 bucket for a year. An analyst now wants to run ad-hoc standard SQL queries directly against those S3 files without loading them into a database cluster first. Which service should they use, and how is it priced?
opts: Kinesis Data Streams, priced per shard-hour
Amazon Redshift, priced per provisioned node-hour
AWS X-Ray, priced per trace segment
Amazon Athena, a serverless SQL query engine for S3 data priced per TB scanned
items.exp: Amazon Athena is a serverless query engine that lets you run standard SQL directly against CSV or JSON files sitting in S3 without loading them into a database, charging only per TB of data scanned.

items.q: A client at Mammoth Capital reports that order checkout sometimes takes 8 seconds. The request flows through API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB -> SNS -> a second Lambda. Every service's CloudWatch dashboard shows normal average latency. Which tool stitches that single slow request into an end-to-end visual trace across all five hops to show which segment took 6 of the 8 seconds?
opts: AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
AWS X-Ray
AWS Organizations
items.exp: While CloudWatch only sees aggregated metrics per service in isolation, AWS X-Ray traces a single request end-to-end across every service it touches, recording timing per segment to pinpoint the exact bottleneck.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's engineers enable Active Tracing on Lambda/API Gateway and include the X-Ray SDK in their application code. They want to attach a customer ID to every segment so support engineers can search and filter X-Ray traces by that customer ID. Should they attach the customer ID as an Annotation or as Metadata?
opts: As an Annotation, because X-Ray indexes annotations as filterable key-value data, whereas metadata is non-indexed and used only for extra context.
As Metadata, because X-Ray indexes metadata for search queries and ignores annotations.
Neither; X-Ray traces everything automatically without enabling Active Tracing or including the X-Ray SDK.
As a CloudWatch CPU alarm threshold.
items.exp: In AWS X-Ray, Annotations are indexed key-value pairs that you can filter and search traces by (such as a customer ID), whereas Metadata is non-indexed context data.

items.q: How do Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray work together in a mature production architecture?
opts: CloudWatch blocks DDoS attacks at Layer 4, while X-Ray encrypts EBS volumes at rest.
CloudWatch sets permission boundaries across accounts, while X-Ray queries S3 files with SQL.
X-Ray replaces CloudWatch completely once you move from EC2 to serverless Lambda.

CloudWatch monitors aggregated health per service (metrics, logs, alarms) to tell you something is wrong, while X-Ray traces individual requests across your distributed system to tell you exactly where.
items.exp: CloudWatch and X-Ray are complementary: CloudWatch monitors overall service health with aggregated metrics, logs, and alarms, while X-Ray traces individual requests end-to-end across microservices to isolate slow or failing hops.

items.q: Mammoth Capital stores 80 TB of uncompressed JSON trade logs in Amazon S3 and queries them occasionally using Amazon Athena. Their monthly Athena bill has grown rapidly and queries are taking several minutes to complete. What change will most effectively reduce Athena costs and improve query performance?
opts: Move the JSON files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Use an AWS Glue ETL job to convert the JSON files into partitioned, compressed Apache Parquet format in S3
Provision a 20-node Amazon EMR cluster running 24/7 to hold the JSON files in HDFS
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
items.exp: Athena charges $5 per TB of data scanned. Converting uncompressed JSON into a columnar format like Apache Parquet with S3 partitioning allows Athena to scan only the specific columns and date partitions required, slashing both cost and query runtime.
items.topic: Analytics Stack: Athena, Glue, Redshift, EMR, OpenSearch

items.q: A healthcare company has built a data lake in Amazon S3 cataloged by AWS Glue and queried via Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift Spectrum. Compliance rules require that data analysts can query the patient table but must be blocked from seeing the 'SocialSecurityNumber' and 'FullName' columns. What is the simplest way to enforce this without duplicating datasets?
opts: Use AWS Lake Formation to configure column-level permissions on the Glue Data Catalog table
Write an S3 Bucket Policy with a Condition block filtering out those two column names
Encrypt the bucket with SSE-C and give analysts only half of the encryption key
Deploy AWS WAF in front of Amazon Athena
items.exp: S3 Bucket Policies operate at the object (file) level and cannot filter columns inside a file. AWS Lake Formation provides centralized, fine-grained table-, column-, row-, and cell-level access control across S3 data lakes for Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR.
items.topic: Analytics Stack: Athena, Glue, Redshift, EMR, OpenSearch

items.q: An e-commerce platform needs to provide customers with sub-second full-text product search supporting fuzzy matching, typo tolerance, and relevance scoring, while also giving engineers a real-time dashboard to search application error logs. Which service fits both requirements?
opts: Amazon Athena
AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon QuickSight
Amazon OpenSearch Service
items.exp: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides real-time distributed full-text search (fuzzy matching, relevance ranking) and log analytics via OpenSearch Dashboards.

opts: Site-to-Site VPN
Direct Connect
Transit Gateway
VPC Peering
items.exp: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated physical network connection from your premises to AWS, offering more consistent network performance than internet-based VPNs.

items.q: To simplify network topology and connect hundreds of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub, Mammoth should implement:
opts: VPC Peering
Transit Gateway
Direct Connect Gateway
PrivateLink
items.exp: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a highly scalable cloud router—a hub that simplifies network architecture by connecting VPCs and on-premises networks.

items.q: Which highly available and scalable cloud DNS web service translates domain names like www.mammothcapital.com into IP addresses?
opts: API Gateway
CloudFront
Route 53
Global Accelerator
items.exp: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's quant team needs to run 100,000 discrete financial risk modeling jobs overnight. They want a managed service that reads the job queue, dynamically provisions the optimal EC2 instances (including Spot Instances for maximum savings), and terminates all instances once the queue is empty. Which service is built for this?
opts: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
AWS Batch
Amazon Route 53
AWS Storage Gateway
items.exp: AWS Batch evaluates queued batch computing jobs, automatically provisions the right EC2 and Spot Instances to execute them, and terminates the instances when the queue drains so billing stops.

items.q: A developer at Mammoth Capital has a Python web application in a ZIP file and wants to deploy it without manually configuring EC2 instances, an Application Load Balancer, an Auto Scaling Group, an RDS database, or CloudWatch monitoring. Which Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) automatically provisions and manages this stack from the uploaded ZIP?
opts: AWS Batch
Amazon Athena
AWS Snowball Edge
AWS Elastic Beanstalk
items.exp: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS where developers upload a ZIP of their code (Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, Ruby, .NET, Go) and AWS automatically provisions and manages the underlying EC2 instances, Load Balancer, ASG, optional RDS, and CloudWatch monitoring.

items.q: What is the core architectural trade-off and use-case distinction between AWS Batch and AWS Elastic Beanstalk?
opts: Batch is for always-on web apps; Beanstalk is for offline petabyte truck migrations.
Batch only runs on-premises; Beanstalk only runs 15-minute serverless functions.

Batch runs queues of bounded, non-interactive jobs (risk modeling, genomics, rendering) that scale to zero when done, whereas Beanstalk is a PaaS for web apps that trades low-level infrastructure control for deployment convenience.
Both are unmanaged hypervisors that require racking physical servers.
items.exp: AWS Batch is built for discrete queues of batch jobs with a defined start and end, while Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS for web applications where you trade granular infrastructure control for automated setup and management.

items.q: Mammoth Capital wants to receive an email alert if their monthly AWS spending exceeds $50,000. Which tool should they use?
opts: Cost Explorer
AWS Budgets
Cost Allocation Tags
Trusted Advisor
items.exp: AWS Budgets gives you the ability to set custom budgets that alert you when your costs or usage exceed (or are forecasted to exceed) your budgeted amount.

items.q: Which tool provides automated recommendations to help optimize costs, increase performance, and improve security by inspecting the AWS environment?
opts: AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Config
Cost Explorer
AWS Pricing Calculator
items.exp: AWS Trusted Advisor is an online tool that provides real-time guidance to help you provision your resources following AWS best practices, including cost optimization.

items.q: To estimate the monthly cost of moving their on-premises workload to AWS before actually migrating, Mammoth should use:
opts: Cost Explorer
AWS Budgets
AWS Pricing Calculator
Billing Dashboard
items.exp: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you explore AWS services and create an estimate for the cost of your use cases on AWS before provisioning.

items.q: Mammoth Capital has 100 TB of historical data to migrate from an on-premises data center to S3, and their internet connection would take weeks to transfer it. Which suitcase-sized, rack-mountable Snow Family appliance provides 80 TB of usable storage per device for standard data center migrations?
opts: AWS Snowmobile (100 PB 45-foot shipping container)
AWS Snowcone (8 TB backpack device)
AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized (80 TB usable storage)
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
items.exp: Snowball Edge Storage Optimized provides 80 TB of usable storage in a rack-mountable, tamper-evident encrypted container shipped via UPS, making it the standard physical migration device for data centers.

items.q: A field research team needs to collect 6 TB of telemetry data in a remote disaster zone with no internet connectivity using a rugged, battery-operated device small enough to fit in a backpack. Which Snow Family device should they request?
opts: AWS Snowcone (8 TB usable storage)
AWS Snowmobile (100 PB semi-trailer truck)
AWS Transit Gateway
AWS Elastic Beanstalk
items.exp: AWS Snowcone provides 8 TB of usable storage in a rugged, battery-operated device small enough to carry in a backpack for harsh edge environments with no internet. (AWS has since discontinued Snowcone and Snowmobile for new orders, but they still appear on older exam material.)

items.q: How do Snowball Edge Compute Optimized and AWS Snowmobile differ in their specialized use cases?
opts: Snowball Edge Compute Optimized holds 100 PB on an 18-wheeler truck, while Snowmobile fits in a backpack.
Both devices require a 10 Gbps internet connection to stream data to S3 in real time.
Snowball Edge Compute Optimized is only for DNS routing, while Snowmobile is for SQL queries.

Snowball Edge Compute Optimized offers 42 TB of storage plus a powerful GPU for local edge ML inference before transfer, whereas Snowmobile is a 45-foot shipping container holding up to 100 PB for exabyte-scale data center migrations.
items.exp: Snowball Edge Compute Optimized pairs 42 TB of storage with an onboard GPU to process data (such as ML inference on video) at disconnected edge sites, while Snowmobile is an 18-wheeler shipping container that moves up to 100 PB for entire data center migrations. (Snowmobile has since been retired by AWS; for very large migrations today you would use multiple Snowball Edge devices or Direct Connect/DataSync.)

items.q: Mammoth Capital has on-premises NFS and SMB servers that continuously generate data. They want an automated, scheduled agent-based service to transfer files between their local storage and AWS (S3, EFS, FSx) at up to 10x faster than open-source tools, with built-in encryption in transit, integrity verification, and automatic retries. Which service fits?
opts: AWS DataSync
AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gateway
AWS Snowmobile
AWS Batch
items.exp: AWS DataSync uses a lightweight on-premises agent to automate and accelerate scheduled file transfers between local NFS/SMB/HDFS storage and S3, EFS, or FSx, handling encryption, integrity checks, and retries automatically.

items.q: Mammoth Capital's on-premises trading desk applications are hardcoded to write files to a local NFS/SMB network drive, and the team wants those files transparently backed by virtually unlimited Amazon S3 object storage without changing how the applications work. What should they deploy?
opts: AWS DataSync with one-time migration scripts
AWS Storage Gateway — File Gateway, which presents a local NFS/SMB share and transparently stores written files as objects in S3
AWS Snowcone
Amazon Athena
items.exp: Storage Gateway's File Gateway extends on-premises storage by presenting a standard NFS or SMB share to local applications while transparently storing the underlying files as objects in Amazon S3.

items.q: Mammoth Capital is retiring its physical magnetic tapes and also has on-premises servers that need iSCSI block storage cached locally and backed up as cloud EBS snapshots. How do Storage Gateway's Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway address these two needs?
opts: Volume Gateway emulates virtual tapes in Glacier, while Tape Gateway presents NFS shares to S3.
Both Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway are offline 18-wheeler shipping containers.

Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block storage to on-prem servers (caching frequent data locally and backing up all blocks as EBS snapshots), while Tape Gateway emulates a virtual tape library that archives tapes to S3 and Glacier.
Neither supports hybrid cloud storage; both are replaced by VPC Peering.
items.exp: Volume Gateway provides iSCSI block storage to on-premises servers with local caching and cloud EBS snapshot backups, whereas Tape Gateway emulates a physical tape library so existing backup software can archive virtual tapes directly to S3 and Glacier.

items.q: Mammoth Capital is migrating a 4 TB production Oracle database from its on-premises data center to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database supports live trading and cannot tolerate more than a few minutes of cutover downtime, and it contains hundreds of complex PL/SQL stored procedures and views. Which combination of services should they use?
opts: Use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) alone to convert the PL/SQL procedures and stream the data
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert the schema and stored procedures, followed by AWS DMS with Change Data Capture (CDC) for continuous data replication
Use AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) to replicate the Oracle database blocks directly into Aurora
Take an offline Oracle backup to an AWS Snowcone device and restore it into Aurora PostgreSQL
items.exp: Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous database migration. You must first use AWS SCT to convert the proprietary schema and PL/SQL code, and then use AWS DMS with Change Data Capture (CDC) to perform the full load and continuous replication for near-zero downtime.
items.topic: Migrating Databases & Servers: DMS, SCT, MGN

items.q: An enterprise wants to 'lift-and-shift' (rehost) 120 on-premises VMware virtual machines running custom legacy Linux and Windows applications onto Amazon EC2 with minimal cutover downtime and without modifying the applications. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
opts: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)
AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
AWS DataSync
AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)
items.exp: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) uses continuous, block-level replication to lift-and-shift physical or virtual servers to Amazon EC2 with minimal downtime.
items.topic: Migrating Databases & Servers: DMS, SCT, MGN

opts: Rehost
Refactor
Replatform
Repurchase
items.exp: Moving from a self-managed database on a VM to a managed database service (RDS) without changing the core application architecture is 'lift-tinker-and-shift' — known as Replatforming.

AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family

AWS Transfer Family
